The Arabs call it a worm [type], and it is dry, beneficial to the body, and its green color is white as coral, black in consistency; it builds up the organs. It has a pleasant scent; when placed in the ear, it induces good hearing and stops bleeding. If swallowed, it relieves bladder pain and cools the body, and has a pleasant fragrance. If crushed and mixed with honey and buried at the root of a tree, it accelerates the tree's natural growth. Cold and dry in the second degree: its water freshens the breath, benefits the sight, relieves paralysis, and if placed among diamonds, it protects against the harm of paralysis. Its extract repels animal poisons, and if its concentrate is applied to the eyes, it sharpens vision, repels cataracts, and eliminates cloudiness.

Marginalia:
Barqaf
Bosansh [note]

It relieves sciatica and is beneficial for the digestive system; it is from the fifth [category], originating from the Indian region. It calms epileptic episodes in women, and if given to a nursing woman, it benefits her.

[Regarding] amchas: Take a moderate amount of Isfahan mint, use it in a dry and cold manner; it is beneficial for the second degree. If used [in excess], it causes the stomach to emit gas, and when cooked, it dries the phlegm in the chest and intestines.

It expels corrupt matter, clears the bile from the liver, and removes corrupt substances; this is stated in the writings of scholars.

When made fresh and ground, [the plant called] Azad Darakhsh is useful as described by the authors; it is known that it is a good antidote to poisons, and it does not cause harm. Wherever it is consumed, it acts as a diuretic, removes hair, and is beneficial for the spleen.

With honey it repels worms from the body, and it is given in the measure of two dirhams. It is cold and moist in the second degree, reduces fever, and has a moderating effect.

But sanbiya [a plant] is of two kinds: one softens and aids digestion, and does not cause harm.

[Regarding] amich: It is first taken with warm water; it is useful against constipation, gout, and senna. It can be taken frequently; it purifies bile and cleanses the body. Mixed with other [substances] it is laxative, and mixed with haldila [myrobalan] it more easily induces gentle laxation.

As for its nature, it is necessarily among beneficial substances whose existence is mandatory; it is among the recognized medicines. It acts as an astringent when taken with haldila, and it destroys worms and dryness.

It is used both externally and internally; internally it is protective. In the brain it causes sneezing, benefits the head, and helps against many dangers.

It eliminates intestinal worms and its extract serves as a repellent; it is of the highest benefit. From the water of Ban there are two varieties: Manū and Anā. The tree of Manū resembles silver in appearance, its bark is like that of silk, and it is fragrant; it is from the highlands of Khurasan among the people there. It treats skin conditions such as herpes, and when dried it benefits vitiligo, blemishes, freckles, skin eruptions, and toothaches; mixed with lemon it is beneficial. Bṭīmīr and dried cinnamon — the fresh form of it was more common before, and it warms and dries; it benefits paralysis, facial palsy, excessive food accumulation in the stomach, and is useful for purging; its resin is of the highest grade; some say it tightens the gums, is beneficial in warfare, thickens bodily humors, and promotes hair growth. Baqam is well known; its fruit is sharp and cuts leeches. In the lands of India and Sind it is very common; it is used in festivals and perfumes, and is employed in various ways. In hot regions it is dry; it benefits paralysis and facial palsy and is useful against cold reptiles and animals; it reduces phlegm; it is known in their lands as māṭarḥ, and from it a fine water is produced. It is used mixed with refined white material; it is warm and dry; it benefits facial palsy, vertigo, and digestion; it dissolves corrupt wounds, removes paralysis, repels insects and animals, relieves dysuria, urinary retention, and is useful for treatment. The blossom of this tree produces an oil, and the oil obtained from it is powerful; it kills worms at sunrise; it purges the bowels, and when this oil is rubbed onto the udders of animals, it causes them to increase their yield, though only by a small amount.

The balsam tree grows in that land, along with roses, sugar, musk, myrrh, and ambergris. It benefits those who use it when rain falls on it, as it draws out the venom of scorpions and provides protection. Every tree that lacks water has no such virtue in place of sugar. The pomegranate with its rind is cold and dry, its skin is used as an astringent, and its juice is beneficial. Its kernels are sweet as honey; the sour pomegranate strengthens the gums. Its peel is useful and aids digestion; its seeds benefit the liver and help with urinary flow. Placing its branches prevents blight, and its virtues drive away bile and intestinal worms, purify the blood, and reduce fatigue.

Abbas reported: I heard the Prophet say, "Eat the pomegranate with its white pith, for it tans the stomach and there is not a single seed that enters a man's belly but that it illuminates his heart and silences Satan's whispering for forty days." When drunk by a noble person it is beneficial; taken with milk it is even better. Mastic mixed with pomegranate is also good.

As for the date palm — it is blessed and greatly beneficial. It aids digestion of food and drink. God Most High mentioned it in the Quran and Hudhayfah reported that the Prophet said: "Honor your aunt the date palm, for it was created from the same clay as Adam." And the tongue in its heart — ask God the Exalted — Gabriel descended with it, and it is at the rank of the blessed tree.

A command was given: take from them all, keeping them in mind, drawing safety from every harm. Regarding peace and greed: apply the ruling — it is narrated that "vinegar is an excellent condiment." And from the Prophet, peace be upon him: "Use olive oil, for it cures pain, removes phlegm, strengthens the nerves, lifts burdens, improves character, gladdens the soul, and dispels heaviness." The oil of the olive tree, if applied to a wound on a tree — the olive tree in particular — and rubbed, will benefit. If a little is applied regularly, it removes pain and is beneficial. Its properties have been recorded: it is used as a remedy and clears head pain. Storax, if taken, removes intestinal worms and is beneficial. When rubbed warmly it is a good remedy. When mixed with fine substances it nourishes and strengthens. When used with Indian pepper it is sought by those who desire it. A little of it mixed together gives strength and is beneficial to the digestion. Adding sugar to it — its oil softens the skin and protects from cold. It relieves inflammation, dryness, and pain, and strengthens the faculties of the brain. Its flesh moistens the teeth and is sought by those who need it. It is cold and moist in the first degree, dry and cold, and is beneficial. If bound with chickpeas soaked in water it is better, and if its seeds are soaked in milk and applied to the roots of a tree and rubbed in the right place on the head, it strengthens hard hair and prevents its falling out.

It removes the bitterness; it is moderately warm and dry, and counters bile-induced diarrhea and weakness. It strengthens the constitution and keeps the temperament restrained and soft. Safarhal is called by name among the cold simples, cold in the first degree. Yahya ibn Talha related on the authority of Dhayba that the Messenger of God gave it and said: "O Muhammad, it heals the heart of sickness and sorrow." And from the Messenger it was reported likewise. It was also reported on the authority of Ja'far al-Tayyar that he gave it and said: "Eat it, for its color and taste are fine." It quells appetite for harmful things, settles fevers, and gives strength to the faculties, and relieves itching. It settles flatulence, and if a pregnant woman eats it, her child will be well-tempered, pleasant-natured, and sweet-smelling. And if a nursing woman drinks it mixed with honey it benefits further, and given to a household it prevents excessive loose bowels, and the seed of the fustuq al-rayr settles coughs. Sabestan is well-known; it benefits the throat, the gullet, and the stomach, and expels black-bile humors. Its ruling: it is astringent, and it is well known that it is cold; it is like stone in its coldness. The mountain tree does not lose its leaves in autumn at all. It strengthens the stomach, gives it vigor, and benefits the intestines from saffron. It strengthens the senses, prevents harm, and is generally beneficial. Sandrus: its tree is well known; its gum is like that of the pine, soft; its heat expels worms in the second degree; and from it a resin is extracted. Oil of Sandrus, known as a constrictive agent, checks epilepsy, hemorrhoids, and [illegible].

It is truly among the most beneficial things — the chestnut (Shah Balut) is well known. In terms of heat and dryness it is less than the oak. Its taste is less intense; it is given to strengthen the constitution and produces dryness. It repels poisons, stops bleeding, and is beneficial for the intestines. The pine (Sanawbar) is well known. Its taste is warm, given to strengthen the constitution. Some say it comes from the larch tree of Khurasan, and others say that it grows in a certain region of the lowlands and hilly terrain. In the wood of the pine there is a resinous substance — when fresh, if a torch is made from it, it burns with great flame and smoke, and its resin resembles mastic; in Arabic it is called the almond of the throat (tonsil). If it is pounded and its decoction drunk with animals and kept, and from its extract a fine paste is made — if gargled with vinegar it removes tooth pain and toothache, strengthens sexual potency, its fumes benefit the nerves, repel serpents, and are useful against scorpion venom. Especially mixed with ginger, walnut, and dates, it corrects the constitution of the muscles. The mountain variety is said to be close to it in nature. It is warm and of moderate dryness; it repels poisons, removes harmful winds from the body, aids digestion, and benefits the bowels. These meanings have been composed in verse. The juniper, used pure ♦ — it is said that it is known to bring forth a stillborn child ♦ — when cut it splits open ♦ — its grit is used in construction. The meaning said is that it is like sugar; others have called it a type of grain and reckoned it among the grains. It corrects straight from the trunk; it is warm, given to strengthen, and expels phlegm and dryness. The Arab scholars have recorded it: it repels weakness, strengthens the organs, and is beneficial in the wonders of creation — mention of which has been made since the time of the Jahiliyya (pre-Islamic era).

The Arabs, whenever one wished to ascertain something in the household, would twist two of its branches together, and when they returned, if the branches remained twisted in the same manner, it was a sign of the chastity of the household of the Shimr family; otherwise it would be the opposite. Jujube (unab) is well known. First degree: it is beneficial for the chest and for nourishing children when used in that way. It is useful for ailments of the eye, stops nosebleeds, and gives freshness. It moistens the back when pressed as a poultice. It prevents the blood. Among the properties of jujube: it stirs the blood when made into a hot infusion and brings it out. It is harmful to the stomach. Oud (agarwood) is well known. Its smoke and fumes repel great poisons and strengthening aromatic pastes. It is dry in the second degree. In the regions where it is used, it serves as a moist agent; it is known that it is made as a good quality product. It surpasses manufactured varieties in this way, as is shown by the fragrance that rises from it. It benefits the heart, strengthens it, and benefits the organs and removes harmful wastes, eliminates winds, calms pain, and soothes the interior. It is called a digestive and is known to be good for the teeth and is pleasantly fragrant. It is of the second degree, better in its aroma and fragrance than pepper. It freshens the breath, strengthens the stomach, and aids digestion. Ambergris (anbar) is of the first degree. Though it comes from Baldūm and however many varieties exist, the closer it is to shore, the better. Aloe (sabar) is raw in its nature. It is placed in houses to be used, and from its flowering, people benefit. It expels what causes grief, and acts as a laxative. It strengthens alertness, and its yellow color is beneficial for children. Mastic (mastiq) is well known and warm.

In sum, it is first dry and cold in temperament, and in Turkish it is called "juwbish"; it is a reliable remedy. Its common use firms up the gums, repels poison from the body, and strengthens sexual desire and potency. It is beneficial for pleurisy, eliminates mucus, and removes blemishes. It purges phlegm from the body, and its oil, when applied as kohl to the eyes, clears cloudiness of vision and removes two close friends [i.e., two ailments]. It drives away fever. Pepper: its temperament is warm and dry, of the first degree. From its worms one should use the bark found among them; the means of pepper is pepper itself, which is warming, and it eliminates cold diseases in the body, and cures night blindness when used as kohl, and is beneficial for the eyes. Applying it as a liniment warms the body, strengthens sexual potency, and pepper relieves palpitations and hardness. It promotes urination and clears cloudiness of vision, aids digestion, and prevents women from conceiving after intercourse. The branches of pepper are known by this name; it is beneficial against cold winds.

Cubeb: it is cold and dry in the second degree, and it soothes grief and pain; it is useful. Red coral: it is warm and dry in the first degree; it eliminates scratching. Its benefit is that it strengthens the liver, and when it is prepared and made powerful, it is beneficial for the spleen. It is effective against freckles, spots on the face, hemorrhoids, and improves vision. Hazelnut: it is well known, warm in temperament, of the first degree. In the Book of Wonders it is recorded that if hazelnut shells are placed in a room, those inside cannot breathe. It nourishes the brain, and its oil, when applied as kohl to a child with blue eyes, blackens the eyes. Pregnant women should grind scorpion [some ingredient] and rub it on [the skin]; it makes the hair grow.

Basil

Cloves heal wounds and improve mental clarity with sugar.
The unripe clove of the tree breaks worms and dryness, healing fractures three times over.
It has the scent of jasmine, freshens the mouth when dry, enhances vision and clarity,
removes cloudiness from the eyes, repels stubbornness, strengthens the mind and memory,
gives strength and relieves congestion; it is better than Chinese cinnamon and similar spices.
Some say it is sought for its properties against paralysis
and related conditions arising from within the heart; it is beneficial and promotes
urination and menstruation, warms the limbs and increases sexual strength,
removes weakness of the limbs. Sugar cane — the pressed sugar of Egypt is better for relieving cough,
chest pain and promoting urination; its fragrance attracts affection and improves complexion.
Its blossom expels mountain worms,
and caraway is beneficial for it; its nature is moderate, it clears the throat,
relieves cough; with jasmine it is compatible, expels black bile, its quality is moderate.
This plant has the mentioned properties; its leaves are balanced and with milk cause
moistening and use of it with sugar warms and is balanced, purifies the liver interior.
Fattens the belly and body, moistens dryness; with ginger, sugar becomes stronger,
and its warmth increases; it resembles pepper in nature, being warm and dry.
Among its second degrees it generates bile, promotes urination and menstruation.
It quenches thirst. The pomegranate tree is among the most beneficial of trees and the tallest.
Its strength is unmatched; upon its branches the serpents do not come; its water is praised.
Its colors are varied and its many types are said to be light and its seeds are numerous.

The disorder of tanalab: from it come several kinds — it falls together and binds like a bond; if naphtha is poured at its root it destroys cavalry, both black and white. If the juice of 'ar and hataq (with nun) of rooster is placed within it along with a pawn, it places worms inside it. If chicken droppings are poured at the root of the tree, it causes the sap to cease flowing and prevents rust, and a liquid drips from it that relieves the stomach's ailment. It is sought so that by this means the digestion is improved. It drives away harm and expels moisture; it relieves headache and clears it. The residue of its water, if boiled and drunk, is nourishing. It sharpens perception, quenches thirst, aids digestion, drives away corrupt food, brings it out through the upper path, fattens the body, and increases appetite for food. It arouses desire, produces semen, expels kidney stones, brings out matter, strengthens the power of desire, and expels what is inside. It benefits the complexion. Those who consume it among young men — their minds remain sound. Fresh young shoots: taken repeatedly they repel fever, expel corrupt matter, stop hemorrhoids, and prevent their recurrence. If pounded and applied as a poultice, it brings benefit. It is among the good foods: it strengthens the nerves, removes roughness, refines the temperament, improves the odor, removes pain, polishes the color. It is beneficial as a medicine; it is beneficial in Khorasan. It increases alertness, strengthens desire, and in this regard the old is more potent. Regarding the tongue: sparrow-water is correct. Its benefit is evident. One draft of its water is correct. In time it expels corrupt humors and corrects imbalance.

Drinking wine frequently and persisting in it brings forgetfulness, trembling, loss of reason, impotence, weakness of eyesight, stroke, epilepsy, and sudden death.

Verse:
Its harms are not few, but know that its benefits are many. Compound.

The Prophet said: Vinegar warms the blood, and the cut vein [benefits from it].
It is cold and dry in the third degree. It cures mange, headaches, and relieves thirst and excessive drinking of water. It is beneficial for dropsy and quenching thirst.

Dry in the third degree, it expels bilious matter and checks vomiting. It reduces body weight, calms the nerves, reduces redness of the face, and diminishes phlegm. It is beneficial in sexual intercourse. It is cold and dry in its degree; its sourness brings many benefits to the back; it sharpens the mind, quenches thirst, settles the stomach, calms bile.

Eating too many of them causes colic. Almonds taken with honey in their shells: if young and unripe, their shell is hard, but they cleanse the chest, dissolve cough, and produce oil. They are beneficial for the eyes, help urination, and relieve colic. Dry and warm in the second degree; with honey they relieve colic.

Taking five or seven of them in water as a drink produces delayed results. Lemon has sharp properties and is useful for repelling poison. It is slightly smaller than a walnut. It is warm and dry in the first degree, and is beneficial for pain of straw [joint pain]; from barley make a staff.

It becomes: the Tabi stone also stops bleeding from wounds, its taste when consumed is like bitter honey, it is not pleasant to the palate, and the white variety benefits the eyes and stops bleeding — it is the Jaraland stone. It is a stone in the shape of a small fish; they place it and bind it upon tumors, and it benefits swellings and afflictions of the groin and buttocks. The resinous stone, Hajr al-Qashsh, is a black stone, denser than coral. From the wonders of creation: if one grinds it and applies even a tiny portion of it to a thousand parts, and if placed on running eyes it stops the flow — this is the Hajr Che of the lower cypress. From the wonders of creation: if ground and held in the hand in flour form, and if swallowed, it benefits. If placed below the crescent, it becomes the Dog Stone — if struck against a stone, it will be repelled far away; likewise, from it one drinks a mirage. And if one blows the ground powder upon it, it will also expel. The Milk Stone (Hajr Labni) is like fire — it gives a clean white color like milk when struck, and its taste is good; combined with a paste it removes cataracts, ulcers, eye irritation, and is beneficial for these. In the letter: when placed on the body and heated, and when brought to the table with food, anyone who eats of that food becomes unable to hold food down, and if brought out from the stomach into water it drives away. The Indian Stone (Hajr Hindi) is a white stone, a compound, and fine powder — it is found on coasts; when placed on a blister it relieves it of water and soreness. And if it is mixed and rubbed on the scalp where no hair grows, hair will grow from it. The Stone Generated from Turbid Water — if certified, it cures epilepsy and madness. The Floating Stone (Hajr Muqawwim ala al-Ma') is a light stone that floats on water.

And it is mentioned that sugar from it was prepared and blended, and brought together in its place, and the taste of Hasan Bahman is like a stone shape.
It descended and in every way it was bound, found in its place, its veins from its stream dried up.
Harsulsun: red and yellow, satisfying, and the best of its kind, like four fine lines.
It goes down into the mine, the sun strikes it, and one removes from its deposit the balance of its gold.
Seven parts of it are dissolved, gathered in the manner of Farakhus, placed where needed, its measure is like that.
It increases, and if it is so ground finely and pressed against it, rubbing it, the benefit increases.
Kharss (Stone): it is refined smoothly, white and pure, heavy, balanced in weight, in the west—
It repels insects and vermin; the charm of Iblis touches the wise men of the valley of Hatim and the people.
It is struck against it, and with it as a companion it does not diminish; Diyati: black, like a full meal of pain.
The black is burnt, and boiled until done, spread on gold, placed on fire, and its surface treated accordingly.
It increases; Nizam stone: white and well-known, quick to act, its juice poured, and a good weight is given to women.
Harm and paleness come, and it becomes mixed with hill-rock; Diyati in its benefit is more excellent.
It brings vitality; Nush: among its properties is that it is placed in the stomach of those who love it from there.
Carrying it brings elevation; Zindalbahar: the foam of the sea and sponge and pain—
It benefits the hair, the skin, the teeth, the gums, the strengthening of the body and the marrow.
It is beneficial; and if bitten by a snake, with it and water poured on the person, salt water is used as a drink.
And from it there is a pleasant smell; Krasnat: and from it a sweet fragrance is given, originating from the root that is heard.
Shanj stone is black, quick and firm; in India it is satisfying to the sight.
It benefits eyesight, repels the flowing of water (cataract), prevents the descent of water, and diminishes worms.
Whoever swallows Sanbi in an infusion it passes through completely, and it comes out dissolved.

It repels and drives away [enemies]; whoever comes near it, the enemy is utterly defeated.
Al-Thum (Garlic Stone): It is a white stone found on the outskirts of dark places, tall in form, green in its veining; it drives away tiredness and protects the sleeper.
It breaks enchantments and dispels troubled dreams. Tarabinus: Found in oil mines and tar deposits; its veining is green, its nature is beneficial; it whitens the eyes with collyrium when applied.
If whitening is desired, it is ground finely and used as a colander-wash, and if cast into water, it benefits.
Every book says it is given to Al-Sud (those of dark complexion); it is ground in Panchaab among the creatures. If one holds it in the mouth, from bitterness and sourness the palate becomes sweet; and if cast into fire, it gives off the scent of ambergris.
The ambergris-stone: it is a mineral, ranked above others in value; it is black, cold, and white; from it comes the scent of ambergris, benefiting those who seek treatment; physicians prescribe its use as beneficial.
Farsalus: It is a black stone; it brings one out of darkness into the light, and when thrown into fire, it ignites and burns with a blue flame; it removes forgetfulness; if carried, a man speaks words of wisdom; it aids memory. If this stone is placed under the pillow, blessed and strong children will be born, with fine features.
If rubbed on the body it cures [ailments]; it is like fire in its energy; it drives enemies away among all creatures. If mixed with poison it renders it harmless; it also benefits animals.
Philqus (Philippus Stone): It is a stone; rub it well and it protects against demons, wild beasts, and enemies who flee from it.
Farunus: It is a stone; applied to wounds, it aids in the growth of flesh with little effort; it brings gold to light; it is found in mines; it is hard in the stomach and the digestive organs.

They consider it proven and effective. If two portions of it are sought, one is freed from delusions and madness. Faryatalsun is found in the land of India. That blood-water and sal ammoniac stone are dissolved in water and applied to that place. Its color is varied, reddish, and it repels thieves. They bring it from the trees; when its juice flows into the water and is made gentle, it speaks well and opens up and proceeds. If one desires that it be beneficial to joints, veins and bones, it is indeed useful. Falqadas: its shape is as they describe, its nature is hot and dry. Third: its properties are like Farmatalsun and it cuts meat like a knife. It is a stone as they describe, brought from the depths of the sea; they make it go through and the stone is ground and brought out. Karami: a light stone, its color is greenish; the wise bring it to the shores of the sea, applied with a reed pen, and they sharpen it. It is used with pomegranate and it repels and Karzabad stone is black and rough, meaning that a file works on it, and a polishing stone grinds it so it becomes white and smooth. It heals. Karsian: a green-colored stone, polished and shaped, cleaned and whitened, made smooth, its teeth cleaned. When dissolved it is standardized, and its color becomes like its kind, and from this Karsian it is taken by itself and it gives. Kark: a white stone like ivory that appears on the shore; they bring it and consider it completely beneficial, and from it snakes and scorpions flee. Karmani: a stone that is like slate and they say it is brought ashore in this state and used as such.

The camel walks and has small dots marked with henna upon it, white — this is lāwaṭā al-ṣūf. It is a light green stone, tending toward the color of pistachio, small and smooth in appearance; it is shaped like a knot of wool. They say it is beneficial for weak eyesight, and when rubbed on flint it produces a knot-like mark. As for lāwaṭā al-aʿẓam, it is a rough golden stone, hard and rough to the touch; if ground and given to one to swallow with water, it is beneficial. As for lāwaṭā al-fiḍḍa, it is a white stone the color of silver; if five dirhams' worth is placed at a distance in water, it draws the water by the force of a magnet. As for lāwaṭā al-quṭn, its color tends toward white with a cottony softness; when ground and placed in water it turns the water white like silver. As for lāwaṭā al-nuḥās, it is a copper-colored stone; if a dirham's weight of it is dissolved and a woman drinks it mixed with water and milk, she will conceive. When placed in a house it repels vermin. Its color is like gold; when placed on the tongue and rubbed on a wall, it produces a brilliant mark. It is a smooth stone with the scent of cucumber; some say it is the stone of Fārs. It is useful for inflammation and is beneficial for treating ulcers. As for lūqmardās, it is found along white rivers; it is used for bloodletting and is beneficial. As for māraṭan, it comes from India; it has been given to sultans and is rare. As for mādūn, it repels the evil eye and is beneficial for the eyesight.

Margin note: This stone is white.

[Bottom:] In the language [of...]

Because it is beneficial to humans and useful against hemorrhoids, it grants relief from piles. Among foreigners and non-Arabs this is unknown. It is cold like a stone, except that it is human and cold. Its first and third degree is dry; it is among the things counted as beneficial, though rare. In the gardens, young unripe girls are bound, and by its property it is said it will not ripen — what belongs to the young. It increases milk production and promotes delivery; rubbing it on the belly helps expel what is inside. In the land of India it is agreeable, and among humans the vulture — how easily it lays its egg. The great ones take from it the birds' benefit and sustain their livelihood all together. It is cold in the first degree and dry in the second, astringent; there are varieties of it resembling small stones. Its contact is soft and smooth and very beneficial; there are many kinds of it and the best is that which has been purified and cleansed by rainwater, like fine sand on rock. It quickly acts on the vessels and passages, and prevents poison from entering the body. And if it does not fully penetrate, they say it is like gray stone — if it is white it dissolves. In the weight of a habasha-measure it makes people dark; if it is black it kills a woman in Habasha. Know that if you seek the benefit of it and if a living creature is found on it, and if any one of them is found — it brings abundance of sustenance; if it is green it brings honor to people. Some of the distinguished ones have doubted this. It is prepared with vinegar as a base, and vinegar is used to reduce it, and it is stored for some time. For the wonders of people, they carry these extraordinary stones, and this account is quoted from Tanthsih-Nama. By God, if the tongue of a stone is applied to a wound, it stops the bleeding and gives much benefit. The red kind — or what resembles it — is used in treatment; it is applied to old wounds and sores and is very beneficial. And in the book of Manshikh it says: this medicine is called Hajar al-Naba — the Stone of Growth.

After God the Most High, the Jewish Stone resembles a walnut of the mountains, and is of various colors. It is found mixed in the riverbeds along the shores, and at the mouths of rivers where they meet, as if the noble one had sought it, strung like beads in a row. It dissolves kidney stones and bladder stones, strengthens the organs, restores health, and prevents certain ailments. If a person drinks from it in a vessel several times over a few days, it greatly increases their vitality.

The reason is that it gathers together the scattered bodily humors and activates the warmth of the sun within the body, and produces fatness and moisture. Its benefits are greatest when it is found in suitable places. If it is red and yellow, and if its power is mild, it will be green, and the stone produced from the union of dead sulfur and pyrite will be red, yellow, green, and white. The green variety resembles green vitriol and talc and alum in appearance, and its taste is somewhat astringent. The yellow variety is medium-sized and gummy in texture, and when rubbed it appears red and white. The Kashkaran and the Zanat are found among them, white and pure, and they are sought in the mountains of al-Jabal and Tabaristan. Together, all varieties of this stone are beneficial for scabies, fistula, nosebleed, and for those who have ingested poison. Two stones rubbed together produce sparks. The stone known as Maghnesar is made from glass. It is constructed from glass and is painted in colors; it is green and from it the cities of Badakhshan make imitation emeralds, and from this material they fashion vessels. This kind of stone is very common in Aleppo and is better and more perfect than anything found in the world. It is polished and when one looks closely at it, it has the appearance of water, and in each of the two waters there is no need. If it is rubbed with quince wine, it will dissolve the stone and expel it.

Fandaj (Alum):
Yellow, red, Hebrew and Abhari varieties, with antimony, are useful for the hair follicles and dispel wind. They relieve hemorrhoids and are used by the people of various regions. Sommost is a black stone, crushed and resembling pitch in consistency, mixed with weight and strength. When mixed it is applied to leprosy — it is said to be useful, giving moisture and healing. It is sufficient for [treating skin conditions], and sulfur is likewise adequate for scabies and similar ailments. It is beneficial for dry and hot temperaments; it treats vitiligo, leprosy, flatulence, and eye ailments. It is useful for removing dead flesh from wounds, and mixed with a sweet substance it is applied. The Persians call it sankraf; it is found in sufficient quantity; it is derived from sulfur and is produced as a worm, and when dried it heals wounds and pains; it keeps meat from putrefying; its stone when crushed is used for fish; it cleanses old [wounds].

Apple (Sib): It is the best in taste and freshness; white ones are moist on the palate and are found in cool, elevated places along the mountain slopes. It stops nosebleeds, menstruation, and excessive flow; it benefits digestion; it relieves heaviness in the stomach; it comforts and removes phlegm; it heals old ulcers.

Talq (Mica/Talc): That is, it is derived from the earth's minerals. It was gathered and refined. It softens and smooths the skin; it is praised by the Commander of the Faithful, Ali (peace be upon him), who said: Talc dissolves [hardness] and softens and polishes.

At the beginning of Rajab, eat it dry three times — it is certainly beneficial for protection. Armenian clay is cold; it is beneficial at the first dryness, astringent to the bowels, and stops blood from flowing from the mouth. For the disease of dimness of vision it is beneficial. Regarding thirst, it is said in the Wonders of Creation: if the pain of the liver increases greatly, drinking wine causes it to flow, and fire breaks out — the flame of the fire is extinguished. Around the foot of the mountain it is bound, and at night it gives light. It is said in the Wonders of Creation: if water is taken from it and the river flows, by God's will, the stone called Qaswur, which is fixed upon the surface of the water in the lands of the Saqaliba, makes it settle, drives away the vapors from limbs, and the flesh of foxes, according to some of the Arabs who sought it, is beneficial. Its obedience is cold at the first dryness, and it grants relief and comfort, and it reduces dryness. It is cooked with meat and used for internal ailments, and it cools and gives light; its nature resists disease and relieves fever and grief. At the first level it fulfills what is needed, and in colors it preserves permanence. Its taste is astringent; it is used for diarrhea and is a remedy for its permanence. Lāwqat al-Dhahab (gold stone): it is a yellow stone, shining like gold on rocks and soil; it grows and is attached inside the skin. It makes those who look upon it feel abundance. Lāwqat al-Sha'r (hair stone): it is a mixed stone, and this stone when rubbed on the body makes the hair grow as normal, and when anointed with tar it makes it grow, and gold flows from it.

Laqat al-Sam — The Greeks call it Sar-i Talis, meaning "flying ember," because when the rays of the sun exceed [a certain intensity], it ignites and flies through the air. If it happens to be black and dark green in color, due to the refinement of its vapors it becomes concentrated in the south wind; its nature in autumn and winter is hot and dry, and if it is in the north, in spring and summer its nature is cold and moist. Satan pursues and follows it, and leads it astray so that it mixes gold, naphtha, charcoal, iron-filings, and all their varieties with sulfur and burns them, so that it grinds them and leaves a residue. If it is placed in the sun, it will not change color or form a pattern. As for leprosy, vitiligo, and white patches, it is beneficial.

Magnet — It is well known. Its nature is hot in the first degree and dry. When its smell reaches the nose it dispels [harm]; if someone wounded by iron comes near it, it draws out the iron. The magnet removes pain from the joints and saves one from poverty; if one acts with it, it nullifies [evil] and every day increases one's dominion. If it is ground and mixed with Armenian red clay and used as a liniment, it is beneficial. If the mixture is excessively strong it induces humility; if it is balanced, it is pleasant in taste.

The Prophet — may God's blessings and peace be upon him — addressed the Commander of the Faithful, Ali, may God be pleased with him, saying: "Expand your soul and from seventy [types] take what is broad in benefit; arrange them in order like crystal, and mention the virtues of your opponents. It has been said he is the gate of knowledge, the liberator of the third [degree], the administrator of the two lights, and the receiver of one soul — and so on."

Minerals and metals — rather, the pleasure derived from them is diminished, and whatever is deficient in them is flawed and unattractive to people. For every one who is more beautiful is a greater witness, just as the Prophet (peace be upon him) said when they came and asked, "Which of you is more excellent, O father of Yusuf?" He replied, "I am the finest of my own kind."

The surplus of the sexual organs overpowers, and whatever it finds suitable it draws toward itself and is gracious and bestows benefit. It breaks out in scabies upon those nearby, and the relief of relaxation is beneficial. The viewing of it from oneself is its strength, and some ancients say it is of Armenian boraq, its nature being warm and dry. It cleans filth from whatever is anointed with it third, and it benefits beauty. It is given in disease as a small amount; it is useful and beneficial for paralysis and facial palsy and other ailments.

Nushadir (sal ammoniac) is well known, and Kafi and Ali Kafi — from its generation as the like of it burns and runs — and most of it comes from the mineral springs; it is white and causes the skin to become uniform. It is warm and dry. In the third degree it is harmful to the eyesight, and beneficial for the unhealthy humors, and useful for paralysis. When mixed with zinc it forms a compound that, when applied, seals the sore.

As for the Hawaniyya: among the subtleties of the air, at the time when the flowing of a certain thing is heard by those present — and it settles — and its wonders are known as "sounding stones," this was mentioned in the introduction, and now in this region it is not cut off. Gaz-angabin (manna) — it is said that in certain regions the air passes over the oak trees and one can hear it, and it thickens. Licorice and sumbul are also gathered. In the province of Kurdistan it is most abundant, and when it settles on the oak tree it is gathered in drops. In that same province it settles on the pistachio tree, and when it becomes well settled, one draws from it two drops. The nature of Gaz-angabin is warm, and...

It is useful for a dry cough, and the ailment settles upon it and passes away. It is obtained in the province of Khwan; it is very plentiful, warm in nature, and it is on the first level. The Elder [plant] — it is very plentiful; those who are known for it follow the path of wind. We mention Isfanaj [spinach]: its ash is like a pen, and if it surpasses in purity, it is useful. As for white lead, it is moderately useful, and for the reason that it gives color to the bread and dough of the pen, it is mixed with quicksilver and rubbed to produce a green-black tarnish which removes impurities. Saba Khan is used in black [form] and is employed for purposes which are beneficial. Qulfdar, with its head and vinegar and wormwood, is established to have properties like those of a fortress. From the burning of needles, one obtains what is not achieved by hot soups alone — it is beneficial and warming. It contracts the belly, and when two parts are tied and that water is placed inside the hollow, mice flee; they run away and swim and also strike and their tension increases. The man calls the snake a "laqabi" [nickname], meaning by it the scorpion, and the tiger and leopard devour it. On its head it is red and white, and in its goodness it surpasses the scorpions of Isfahan — it is spotted. Its saliva removes blotches and blackness of the skin, and dripping it upon the ear is beneficial. For washing it should be performed perfectly with gum and the use of male arsenic from its interior is excellent. Eating it settles the heart and its properties establish that it is a mineral, and transfer of the goat [substance] — whatever is written in other books about its green essence is transmitted from here, and it is among the created things. Chapter Nine: A thief who steals from villages, in medical texts, treatments are given, and confinement in the earth is imposed. The air of summer and its temperate quality comes from the subtle and light [elements], and nourishment is given. The cold wind of the land of men arrives, and bile and [the other humors] return together.

The form of the tapeworm is like a worm; breaking it with vinegar stops diarrhea, urine, and menstrual bleeding, and it is a diuretic. It retains appetite, expels melancholic waste, cleanses, and warms together. It purifies and clarifies, and its vapor is known for women's ailments. It is astringent and each of its red-colored ones, taken with wine, is strengthening; it is cold and dry in nature, astringent, and settles bile until the worm cannot appear or spread.

The lesson: wheat is like fermented milk in nature; when dried and broken, it is mixed together and used once a year for planting. Every few years it gives off bran and purified flour; it relieves kidney and bladder pains. It is useful; the leaf resembles adabi in shape, except in some aspects. When the wind blows it, it gives shade, and the nightingale is named after it; some also call it by the name "mu'izzi." It is known as jasmine, both white and yellow, and its shrubs are slender; when dried it loosens phlegm, and is useful for paralysis, sciatica, and difficulty urinating.

Second form: a mention of things from within — certain trees, like the cypress and juniper, are noted; they are similar in that they dry moisture and are used for poplar. They are also counted among the hard substances; their firmness and solidity establish good qualities. 

Note: Asafetida mixed with meat firms the teeth and improves the mind's clarity. The galbanum is a known resin, useful as a remedy; it treats headache and relieves pain. It is cold in nature, and the mother-of-grape tree is one that needs much water and is widely known.

It makes the breath pleasant; its gum, pounded like Arabic gum, is applied in abundance over wounds, purifies the blood, and gives luster to the complexion. It is a thorny tree found in the mountains of Fars and Luristan. At first its nature is temperate; its milk, when boiled, repels vermin and worms, drives away pests and malignant things, heals wounds and putrid flesh, removes obstructions, and expels phlegm. It promotes urination and is beneficial.

Arwan: A tall, straight tree whose blossoms resemble white elder flowers; its nature is cold. A small amount strengthens the heart, clears the eyes, brings joy to the spirit.

Sun: A tree found in the mountains, resembling tar in its properties, from which resin is extracted. It is said that shelter may be taken beneath it; some say it is like the milk tree. It heals worm-damaged flesh, binds broken limbs, benefits the fourth organ, and when applied to the teeth relieves toothache. Fresh wounds benefit from it. Rubbing the gums with it is good for the teeth. Its gum, when dissolved, is beneficial as a remedy.

Its juice, when drunk, expels phlegm from the body; it aids digestion and improves the breath; rubbing with it is beneficial; its wood, boiled, first expels wind, aids digestion, improves odor, and its sap taken in doses from the first to the second measure, nourishes and steadies the body; one who rubs it on the head is cured and benefits. Another use: pound it and apply to the painful gums — it is called Khanzaran; its wood and bark are used thus.

Hawkan

The sap of the plane tree (chinar) is red and correct; its properties are like pepper in effect.
It is called "orzā" — it is a great tree, and its fresh, unripe fruit
[Remedy of the Quran]
has not yet ripened; it expels foreign matter from the body, and with vinegar it removes vitiligo and heals wounds.
Wounds it benefits and brings remedy; it relaxes the body's weak organs and bones.
It is tied because it sets the broken bones of the spine, reduces swelling and dryness of the joints.
Second benefit: It is useful for facial paralysis, weakness of the limbs, and numbness; it benefits the heart of the chinar.
The chinar is the greatest of trees in size, and the longest-lived; they have said it lives very long and grows to great height.
It has been recorded that a chinar in Azerbaijan lived — it was said — as many as one thousand years, reaching immense age.
It was ancient and standing since time immemorial, and because of its great age it was venerated like an idol.
It gave shade to the chinar grove, pleasant to the heart; in the morning it accepted the presence of travelers from every direction.
I said to it — kindly and with affection — "You have made the heart live again, like one who was dead."
The great trunks between its branches spread wide; its insects buzz and swarm around it.
Its smell is fine, and its flavor — if chewed — is beneficial for the teeth.
Its temperament is cold and dry in the first degree. Galbanum (jāwshīr) is a tree that becomes milky.
It is useful against decay in the first degree, and in the third degree it dissolves phlegm and warms the womb,
and it matures hard swellings and dissolves them, and dispels raw humors from the body,
and it is useful for sciatica, pain in the hips and loins, for hernia, and it relieves urinary retention.
It is warm and dry in the third degree; it strengthens the stomach and restores its vigor, and dispels wind.
Binding it tightly stops bleeding, induces sleep. Ash-tree (ishtaʿār) is a cold tree.
Its resin is warm and dry in the second degree; its branches in terms of their effect are useful.

It has roughness and repulsiveness; it is used for joint pains and sciatica. It helps with difficulty urinating, difficulty in childbirth, fetid odors, and flatulence. The winds it suppresses are those of the stomach. If a woman suffers pain in childbirth, its juice is used, and similar things ease delivery. Dal — In some regions it is of the nature of a plant whose juice is used in treating anal pain; put water on it, it opens the urine and repels the venom of animals. The poets know it.

Extracted from a certain source: Arbeh — it is well-known; its juice is used in buildings and is greatly beneficial; it is used in construction and for fine craftsmanship. Women make food from it, as it is light and fully nourishing.

Sarw (Cypress) — It is well-known; riders and foot soldiers use it to free themselves. The proverb says: "Like the cypress of Lahore, upright; it came of itself, fresh and dry." It strengthens the organs and is durable and beneficial. Its two uses are well-known: it is useful for those with difficulty urinating and it relieves pain, settles odors, and if its bark is crushed, it is useful for kidney stones.

Summad — It is a tree; its bark is used as a lozenge for the stomach, and it is suitable for bringing on menstruation. Shmad — it is well-known; it is used frequently, and it is known from certain sources to be used in cases of constipation. It is a tree; it is used widely; it brings out blood and relieves diarrhea. There is nothing better for treating the throat; it is useful for ulcers, joint pain, vomiting, and bloating. Keeping it on one's person repels the stench of the Abyssinian. Sandal (Sandalwood) — well-known.

Arshamuna — the Persians call it "hand" — is found in the land of India. Its branches are red and white, and its whiteness diminishes cold. Its taste is cold and dry. The second degree breaks obstructions, is beneficial for mange, and treats palpitations, convulsions, and delusions, and reduces swellings and inflammations. It is called "salanj." The resin of its tree solidifies worms, and the first-degree gum repels bodily humors and gives strength, disperses thick winds, stops trembling, epilepsy, and paralysis.

The salm tree is a wind-worshipping tree; the sal tree likewise.

Its mention and its reports are widespread. Tarkhun is found in the region of Farghana. Tarfa: know that it is a tree — the first-degree gum is beneficial, drying things up, and in warm regions it provides much relief. It is not fit for men of little vigor. In its shade, gardens are established but it is not good for tender vegetation. It does not come near fine plants. Its old [resin] extracts from the root — they call its dates "khurmash" — it is cold. The second and third degrees are useful for chronic diarrhea, stop menstruation and discharge, are useful for pain of the ear, toothache, and earache, and relieve cold in the head.

"Hildi" — David's remedy — its white milk is beneficial. "Arab" — meaning Arab tribes raided and plundered it, and used it to smear heads. It is useful for wounds. Applied to fresh wounds, it is beneficial; it is an astringent fragrance.

"Narbaychijanm" — the "Ushsha" tree — in the land of Farnia it is called "Oud al-Salib." It breaks worms, is drying, the third-degree gum promotes urination and menstruation, takes away fever, reduces swellings, and when pressed, it stops pain.

Gout and indigestion and nightmare — it is beneficial; do not exceed fifteen grains.
Kharzad: Euphorbium (farfiyun) — according to some authorities it is a plant, and according to others it is a manufactured substance, dry and hot.
The fourth: it is aromatic, and alone it is beneficial for phlegm; with honey it warms and strengthens the head.
It brings warmth and dryness, strengthens the joints and the stomach, and fortifies them.
It settles pain, and together with vinegar is beneficial for the spleen; it repels worms.
When it is burnt it is weak; boiling it with vinegar and colocynth eliminates worms and brings relief.
It is useful for itching; boiled with vinegar it repels mange; it is known as katras.
Samal and farwah and sitanr: it is beneficial and purifies the channels.
It causes constipation; approaching the heart, it is necessary for the body as stated.
By its nature it is soothing; it is easily laxative and it raises the voice.
It commands the liver and the stomach and raises the rank of one who drinks it.
It breaks down and refines; from the species of reed it is counted.
It is beneficial in a dry state; another type of it arrived.
The worm dries out; it nourishes and settles; it is an aid to the constitution.
Blood it stops; it makes smal fit; it produces warmth and feeds the body.
Asafetida: it aids digestion; another is called mudabbil al-jism, another mudabbil al-'ayni — found in the land of India.
Its ash as a poultice is correct and sound; it is like plaster, dry.
Third: it relieves palpitations; it is beneficial for opium; it strengthens the heart, clears yellow bile.
Thirst, narrowing of the mind, faintness, weakness of the stomach — it repels all these.
Another is called mudabbil al-shuhur; it is also known as akish — eaten with onion it repels pain.

It relieves wasting disease (consumption) and retention of urine. Camphor comes from a pine-like tree; camphor is cold and dry in the third degree. When it is like the khayir tree it is pressed and collected. From camphor comes also something the common people use to stop discharge, for beautification. Camphor in its own right: the people of the Najd region, those who know the camphor tree, recognized it; and camphor, according to some, comes from its own wood from a cypress, and that is the best kind; and according to others, it is obtained by boiling and breaking it up, and that is of middle rank — it drives away heat and benefits the humors. It is obtained from those camphor trees and in the sea it is used, dried and preserved. Of camphor in the sea its nature strengthens: it stops nosebleeds and cold fluxes in the brain, and it expels excess matter and benefits the flesh. It is useful for preventing burns and for repelling the poisons of worms.

Karkān: Tablets are made from it; frankincense and worms and tablets — it has benefits. It strengthens the heart and drives away wind and removes weakness of the stomach, and stops the discharge of blood in old chronic cases; it is beneficial for cold fluxes, rheumatic pains, and chapping.

Lā Blā: It is a mountain tree, warm and dry. Its resin is a great laxative and brings on vomiting, and has a pleasant scent. Even if one eats it with honey, the honey becomes harmful. If ants fall upon that tree they perish. Flies that land on it also die. When a dead creature falls into water near it, the water becomes unclean.

Lisān al-ʿAṣāfīr (Bird's Tongue): It is a cultivated tree; its bark is used [medicinally]. It nourishes those who eat it and gives them strength; the first grade is the best. It warms and softens.

Māmīrān: Warm and dry. The third grade is an emollient; it is placed as a plaster and used as a stick. It removes diseased nails and corrupted flesh, and what remains is preserved.

[On mastic:] Mastic is the resin of a tree, dry and small in quantity. It strengthens the stomach and digestion, repels phlegm, and stops bleeding. It freshens the breath and improves the taste of the mouth. [On myrrh:] Myrrh (muql) also similarly suppresses bad odor. It calms the nerves and soothes the eye. It has been mentioned by Abu Sahl al-Ayn and others. It has several properties: it is mentioned among the remedies for pain in the side, for treating disorders of the body, and for scrofula and similar ailments. Its temperament is moderate. It tends toward warmth and dryness. It is gathered in winter and in arid regions from green shrubs. It is known by the name "dukhar" in some places. It is oily and viscous when extracted. [Second form:] As for what has been said before regarding its use — it is worthy of praise in the right time and measure. Whoever is able to prepare it can make something beneficial from it; its properties are well-known to physicians and the wise. Its temperament and properties are blended together, and its benefits are numerous and varied across different ages and peoples. The Almighty Creator — may He be exalted and sanctified — spoke in the Glorious Word: "Look then at the effects of the mercy of God, how He revives the earth after its death" — verily in that is One who gives life to the dead, and He is over all things capable. Scholars differ on various points: some have said that every living thing standing on the earth is sustained by it, and everything on earth returns to it, and the dwellers therein — as from the Glorious Word.

He said: "Do not approach this tree." Some say: For this reason the fig is noble — except that one should not eat near it, for it causes nausea among the trees and barley. For every stalk, leaf, and branch remains in place for several years, and I and its bark and all its branches do not decay — it is a tree, and what strengthens the veins and the sun-like branches, keeping them together. From ripening it is best, and this quality is most suited to the chest, and its properties are mentioned. From the arrangement by which the noble essence can be understood through the method of letters in four: warnings and two layers and poisons and others — let us mention them with God's help, the Exalted — Foods. Every day consuming hunger in full measure does not harm; from it a watery humor is produced. It quickly causes looseness of the bowels; as long as the property of the remedy remains empty, it will be so. From the fruits of those mentioned, producing wind and settling it: rice is hot, beneficial for the first degree; dry is the second degree and is blessed; consumed with milk it is better than whey, moist. The continual use of rice — eating it roasted, cooking it fine, and thinning and reducing it — makes sleep good, reduces deafness, and does not cause pain in the tongue and mouth with its smoke. Warm and dry in the second degree, and some say it is cold and dry — it is useful for weakness of the stomach; continued consumption of it stirs up corrupt humors. It drives away two kinds of intestinal worms, leeches, hemorrhoids, and crabs from the teeth. It is known: first it is pounded and the skin is removed, wanting fresh — cold and moist in the first degree; dry is cold and dry; the essence of both is present. One must look into its increase — it produces fever in the heart and when heated causes mange. It is the shell of a nut, but if it is unripe it harms and corrupts and disturbs, and if it is given to domestic birds to eat, as if they had tried, they flee from it.

It removes blemishes of skin, lentigo, freckles, and dark spots, and carries away troublesome roots and growths; it soothes pains and brings relief.

Spinach (Isfanaj): It is well known, cold and moist in the second degree. It is beneficial for headache and back pain, useful for roughness and inflammation of the chest, and calms fever. It is laxative. Taken in the weight of a mithqal with vinegar, it is useful for the first stage of pleurisy and for chest diseases and coughing; its smoke extinguishes burning pain and aches. Combined with honey it relieves skin conditions and cleanses the complexion. When eaten with pepper and honey, it is of much benefit in strengthening the body. It is useful as a corrective for the third degree, and moistens what is overly dry. If chewed, it prevents bad breath, and if its sweet water is made into a syrup with honey and taken, it improves the vision of the eye. If one takes it and eats it for seven days, it increases the vital spirit, repels palpitations of the heart. If a few drops of its juice mixed with onion water are put in the ear of a person as mentioned, it removes pain. If its juice is drunk and kept inside, it repels the effects of poison, reddens the blood, expels corrupt blood from the veins, is useful for hemorrhoids, prevents the descent of water into the eye, strengthens sexual potency, and if mixed with oil of sesame it heals fistulas, whitens the pupils of the eye, eliminates what is harmful, changes the color of hair to black.

Watermelon (Battikh/Kharbuzah): It is cold and moist in the second degree. If its seeds are few it is colder, and some say its seeds contain worms. If one eats it with honey, this is extremely beneficial for the bladder. The people of Khwarazm say it loosens the joints, so that it is said it softens and relaxes them like the sinews of a camel. Those who eat much of it along with vinegar will find that it suppresses it entirely. It benefits menstruating women. The watermelon cleanses the tongue of the mouth, and warms the cold liver...

It distributes its freshness and its cold vapor returns the heat, and if it falls warm into the Persian Gulf, the waters of Kerman mix with it, and that water settles in the Persian Gulf.
Also another product of Kerman: for one year the sea was low, and Abu Hurayra reported:
The Prophet (peace be upon him) said regarding fruits, the watermelon is to be cherished and savored, and God has made it so:
The sweetness of the watermelon surpasses the sweetness of honey for one who eats of the watermelon; God has made it a blessing,
And it removes a thousand hardships and lifts grief. For many years, people
would take watermelon seeds and a light would come from them illuminating like a lamp,
And those afflicted with paralysis were greatly helped by it.
It settles the stomach and increases strength, and the passages it opens upward, and it digests quickly,
And it cleanses the blood vessels and the humors, and purifies corrupt mixtures from the body.
It softens the phlegmatic humor, improves the smell of the mouth, and removes the unpleasant smell,
And it clears skin blemishes, soothes sunburn, and relieves bilious headaches and tongue ailments.
The people of Arabia, the fellahin and the learned, count it among the most beneficial of things.
This is the Khorasani variety: it contains no worms, and no insects dwell in it,
It settles the stomach and dissolves obstructions, expels roundworms, and breaks them up.
If it is eaten when the moon is beneath the earth, it will cause the milk to smell unpleasant.
And to dispel the coldness of phlegm, when pounded with honey and applied,
It reduces pain, drives out poison, and slowly penetrates the body's depths.
It gives pleasure and beauty, removes blemishes, and on an empty stomach taken daily it is a remedy.

It is beneficial for loosening the bowels, and when the teeth are treated with it a second time, it prevents the spread of wounds and poisons. One gives it mixed with honey, after purging with aloes, and if after two hours the smell of garlic comes from the mouth, they consider it sufficient, and no more is needed. It disagrees with those who are unwell, and eating garlic makes one hear a ringing sound. If one applies a mixture of its fat to the hair, it benefits the hair greatly.

Jawars (millet): it is well known; some scholars call it "dukhn" and others call it "labiya." It grows in the throat, its smoke reaches the lungs, its taste is cool and mild, it soothes soreness of the throat and pains, and it suppresses coughs. It acts as a general sedative for pains when taken seasonally. The Arabs called it "buhqan" — eating it makes one somewhat intoxicated; it soothes pain in the first instance, suppresses aches, and every time it is eaten it sedates pains and relieves them. The Commander of the Faithful Ali, peace be upon him, said: "Eat jirjir (arugula) whole, for it benefits the stomach." They cook it in pomegranate juice with pleasant spices, and then take it with honey, sugar, and almond oil — this is beneficial and agreeable. Asafoetida relieves headache, except that eating it is somewhat harmful at first. Fumigating with it, and anointing with it mixed with oil of ben-nut, cures certain conditions. Taking it with honey water every day in the amount of a few dirhams, making it a habit, is useful. The best of it, according to Muhammad, is the fresh kind; one fumigates the dead with it — it is cool and dry in temperament; taken with sugar it is pleasantly sweet, good for digestion, and known to be nourishing. However, it is harmful when eaten raw; in autumn it is light and dry. Taken with sugar it opens the bowels, promotes urination, and strengthens the constitution, though it is not nourishing in the manner of dense foods. It generates flatulence, and when taken it produces phlegm and black bile, relaxes the body, and is known to strengthen the teeth.

It is warm and dry; it promotes digestion, gives vigor, and is beneficial for the body. From it the horse receives news — it is called "kharf." Sindan, when chewed, is warm and dry. Third: it sharpens the mind and gives vigor, and makes fire strong upon hair. It is beneficial for mange, sciatica, and friyā, and for dispersing abscesses; it repels vermin. Hulba (fenugreek): it increases warmth and dryness, is good for joints, and is wholesome. It gives back what was lost, increases vigor, and its fluid is white. It nourishes, increases hair with myrtle, augments the spirit, and its mark remains on the body. It is acidic; it illuminates the interior, removes dryness, and drives away rheum. It is beneficial for the nerves, relieves pain, is wonderful for mange and fevers. Applied as a coating, it extracts the juice of māsh (mung beans), cools jaundice, and repels worms. It is red and beneficial; it heals wounds, preserves health, nourishes the spirit, and the body. It strengthens the teeth and gives vigor. Wheat: the Arabs regard it as blessed and more agreeable than barley; it is well-digested and of moderate temperament. It is the first and best; it is the sweetest and the most nourishing of breads, however many there be. It is not harmful, its bread is pleasant, and chickpeas are wholesome. It is reported that since the time of Adam, peace be upon him, the people of paradise have been fed upon it. Sesame: it was taught to the people. They learned how to harvest wheat, how to bring it from the threshing floor to the mill, to grind and knead it. So it has been passed down from the time of our father Adam. In the time of Jamshid it was like a house with two doors, and in that age...

We are aligned with the domestic [remedy], and at the time of Moses the great master said: we came to know the self is great, now listen:
In this region the path of Islam — come, so that in truth one may behold the awe of divine majesty —
The author of the book says: compliance with the honored religious law and its sanctity are sufficient proof and reason; it is wondrous in this age.
When one laments and the time comes, it brings benefit and gives strength; the self does not diminish, and it increases the power of virility.
It benefits all the limbs, repels harm from the head, expels corruption, dissolves phlegm, breaks up hardness and stiffness.
It is white, dispels jaundice, clears biliousness, settles the stomach, and is astringent in a moderate degree.
It is dry, increases moisture, quenches thirst, stimulates the kidneys, and is diuretic.
It strengthens [the body], and what is called "wheat of Iran" — one ratl of honey and one ratl of water are mixed together and boiled, and it produces semen and benefits [the body] over time, causing emission.
It is known to have the strength of wheat, and promotes urination and is viscous; it is further said —
The Persians call it "isfand" and the Arabs call it "wild rue" [harmal].
One takes it with henna-water; it makes the complexion ruddy, like a pomegranate skin that has been stripped — it increases firmness, subdues [phlegm], and is beneficial.
For the joints and for sciatica, its extract is beneficial for the teeth and the gums.
It is useful, and even more so: one grinds it and smells it [inhales it] — [marked: special note].
Lettuce [kahu] is cold and astringent; it is heavy and when eaten it numbs [the senses] and suppresses [appetite].

The leaves of the plant are finer; they stop bleeding and correct disorders of the brain.
If dissolved in wine and taken, it improves vision, promotes good circulation and eye health,
but it is harmful to reproductive vigor; when women consume it mixed with the sap of a tree, it reduces men's potency.
Its gum, if mixed with sulfur, acts as a poison. Khakhash (poppy): it is cold and dry in nature.
It increases semen production; its white and black varieties are useful; its extract resembles Egyptian gum arabic.
Opium: it is cold; when taken in the fourth degree, it suppresses and causes heaviness and headaches in all things.
Especially it burns like fire; its water and steam are harmful to the head and pain — it is beneficial for the head.
It is correct and harmful; it diminishes the constitution; there are many disadvantages in consuming it.
Also it is called Hilbān and Khatā; it is also called Samandaras.
It is beneficial for snakebite; Rāziyānaj (fennel): it is mild.
Fourth degree: it is companion to travelers and desert dwellers; it is praised; it drives away wind.
It expels phlegm, reduces eye discharge, cools animals and keeps the eye fresh.
It increases women's milk, repels worms in fresh form; Rabās grows on walls.
It is cold and dry; the fourth grade, from ancient times among lightning-struck and those struck by thunderbolts it is deadly.
It is beneficial against dryness, plague, typhoid fever, dysentery, and fainting.
It improves sight and brings back freshness; it is found in China.
It is rough in sight; when dry it corrects diseases according to medical judgment.
It benefits the intestines, blood, appetite, and signs of the body, expels phlegm.
It relieves breathlessness and benefits; Silq (beet): it is cold and dry.
Its water is moderate and its nature is mixed; it cools the body, removes freckles, skin blemishes, and facial discoloration.

It is noteworthy that its extract kills lice, and again its residue clears away phlegm. In the region of Tabaristan it is used as a poultice. All its parts are used as an antidote to poison; it kills worms and is straightening. First, if its leaves are rubbed together with oil and the hair is lengthened, it helps with chapped skin and promotes digestion. It is beneficial and, when mixed and pounded together, it increases monthly flow. It increases dill; it dries up bad moisture and removes piles, darkens vision, brings sleep, relieves hemorrhoids, fear of the heart, and palpitations, and ailments of the blood. But it reduces semen production. Poetry says: it is right and dry.

It is suitable for warm and cold temperaments, and for young people with cold temperament it is grilled. It provides nourishment, and boiled with wheat it becomes beneficial. It is narrated from the Commander of the Faithful, Ali, peace be upon him... Among the most refined things, it is said that when Adam, peace be upon him, was brought down, he took it in his hand. It remained in the hand of Adam, peace be upon him, as a grain of wheat was given and taken from his hand. It is among the finest of foods and in general it is beneficial for ailments. It expels bilious substances and prevents flatulence.

Turnip (shaljam): its Arabic meaning is known; it is cold and moist in the second degree. If it is not fully ripe, it is prepared with honey, pomelo, and mixed; it makes the turnip sweet. It produces semen and increases it, gives good milk, and provides nourishment. It increases sexual desire and is useful. It is well known and good for the bladder. If it is broken and it turns out to be dark and black, do not eat it at all; and if it is white, it is cold and dry.

The third humor: it is beneficial for acute pains, headaches, colds, and stopping bleeding. It reduces [certain conditions], thinness of the body; its oil warms the cold of winter. It is a remedy for ear pains and is useful as a medicine; it kills worms and insects. The third remedy: soaked in water and applied in the house, it cools the entire body. It removes lice; washing with soap mixed with turmeric brightens the skin and removes blemishes. It repels insects and small crawling creatures; tarragon worm removes dryness and moistness. It eliminates gas and strengthens digestion; it brings out food and dispels winds. It is useful for skin diseases, vitiligo, colds, and pains. It is useful for bile; it regulates the flow of bile and binds the looseness of the bowels. It is useful for tightness of breath and brings on menstruation. Tarragon: it is warm and dry; it removes pain from the throat, strengthens potency, and freshens the breath. Lentils: they are cold and moist; their harm is that they cause poor vision. They are harmful to the stomach; they produce heat in the eyes. They are useful when cooked with aromatics; they nourish and provide strength. Continuous use causes heaviness in the head. Radish: it is warm and slightly dry. Continuous eating stimulates digestion, strengthens potency, and expels poison. It induces belching, brings out phlegm, and is useful for clearing the throat and the head. It relieves headache and toothache, and its juice...

He brought it and I treated the jaundice, and the yellowness of the jaundice was remedied by half a day's portion. It benefits the eyesight and increases vision. In the land of Habra, sandal wood was not well-ground and the water of the date-palm was bountiful throughout the region. The hare's food prevents digestion and draws out the bile in a great quantity. It is not digestive, and among its properties it is suitable for those who need it, and it is called by the Arabs "al-naqliyya al-muhaqqa." The third and second types increase heat and dryness, if one is found among the horses and its people do not have nocturnal emissions, it increases with each occasion. Ground and mixed with honey, applied to the urethra and to inflamed areas, it is beneficial for headaches, eye inflammation, hemorrhoids, toothache, and serpent bites. The cucumber is cold and moist in the second degree. If it is well-shaped in appearance and its form is as described in the books of natural philosophy, and if it is taken at the time of its harvesting in the presence of pure water, and if it falls with the scent of blood it is found beneficial. The juice of the cucumber is cold in nature and removes bile. It has many benefits. The juice of the watermelon removes heat from within. The second type, eaten with honey, clears the urine slightly and returns the constitution. If one gargles with honey mixed with it, it strengthens the liver and spleen and is cooling. The Arabs call it by its own name; it is cold and moist in the second degree.

The section: Honey mixed [with it] prevents sweet [things], checks that, and is beneficial. It was said like Paul, coming from speech, like a rushing stream. Before it the gourd tree substitutes for the vine, and it does not give it a throne; the gourd repels bloating, maintains the stomach, expels worms, and is beneficial for hemorrhoids. It has been noted as useful. He who sought it: the third degree is moist, and the wax of the world is in its nature. It settles wasps; if one partakes of it, the darkness of the body is removed and head troubles are relieved. It dispels disturbing visions and protects against hemorrhoids, strengthens the legs, and purifies. Ibn Khaffan said: it expels phlegmatic colic and relieves pain. The mountain variety was sought at the second degree of moisture. It heats the chest, relieves congestion and colic, and expels pain from the loins. It is well known and has been noted. Aloes: its taste is at the first degree of moisture, good for gilding, removing rust and roughness of teeth; boiling it in the house repels snakes, and it counters thick phlegmatic bile. Asafoetida (anzarūt): coriander is cold and dry at the first degree. It is suitable and should not be used with food that harms the brain; if used with onion it is beneficial for difficult childbirth. When taken as a drink it removes darkness of the body, weakness of the limbs; its juice applied with snakeweed burns the tongue. It repels snakes, scorpions, and other vermin from the house. Coriander is known among the Arabs as juljulān; it is cold at the first degree and hot; it soothes burning sensations. Celery (karafs): it is warm and dry at the second degree; it is well known.

It increases sexual potency, prevents seminal emission during intercourse, dispels flatulence and palpitations.
It benefits the stomach, promotes urination, expels worms from the intestines, reduces belly swelling, and is known as cress in some regions.
Fenugreek (hulba) is well-known; it is warming and dry, beneficial for the region.
It relieves flatulence and palpitations, strengthens the stomach, promotes urination,
and reduces belly worms. Cumin likewise is known: it aids digestion, relieves symptoms, and is moderately warming.
The second type: its urine and excretion, along with its foods and digestion, are beneficial.
When a mouse urinates on fire, it purifies the air; it is known to benefit Egypt and beyond.
It stops nosebleeds when placed on the head, and relieves chest complaints.
It relieves palpitations and tightness of breath. The first type is warming and dry.
The second: in the belly of the camel it remains, it warms the stomach and dispels worms.
It is useful against paralysis, smallpox, fistulas, ulcers, and it resolves the humors.
Lubiya (kidney beans): well-known, warming, and it consolidates. It primarily dispels the humors.
It increases sperm and blood; it is harmful for postpartum bleeding and fattens the body.
Urine of certain animals is harmful. Mash (mung beans) is well-known; some Arabs
call it cold and dry; it is beneficial primarily for the heart, as some say.
It is nourishing, brings benefit, and is useful for the organs and limbs.
But it reduces sexual potency when consumed in excess and weakens the body. Nankhuah is well-known,
and dry; it benefits the body's members in the third degree, quickly relieves vitiligo and leprosy.
Coriander repels humors, reduces swelling of the abdomen, is useful for the skin and spleen.
It promotes urination and relieves poisoning. Tafnij is well-known: warming and dry in the first degree.
The second type: it is a long worm, strengthens the stomach, and reinforces the powers. God knows best.

It increases [vigor], and if a pregnant woman engages in intercourse she will not remain pregnant, and the juice, if one refrains from eating it with pomegranate, will settle the digestion.

Hailun: In general, the pomegranate warms the body and gives firmness and is wholesome to eat. It gives desire, increases semen, dissolves poison, opens obstruction, and water dripping from it is good for the eyes. It is good for the gums and for clearing phlegm, and boiling it with sugar is excellent. If it strikes the head and expels the venom, the patient will recover.

Hindba (Endive): Wild and cultivated chicory is cold in the first degree and moist in the second. It is a remedy for every ailment. Some call it the "trust of the believer." It is mentioned by Ali the Scholar in his complete work. The water of Lebanese sand mixed with it removes jaundice and heated conditions. It moderates the heartbeat, relieves palpitations, and benefits those with liver complaints. It is cold and dry in the first degree; it counteracts poison, expels worms, is good for quartan fever and toothache. If one is afflicted with melancholy it is beneficial. A decoction of chicory with meat broth taken over a year's course will benefit those with complex ailments described in the Book of Wonders.

Note: At this time it is known, and among the names by which it is called, the most common is recorded in Greek and Hebrew. It is also known by other names and is mostly known in Arabic and Persian by famous names arranged alphabetically.

Idhkhir (lemongrass): It is warming in the second degree and dry in the first. It is a solvent and balancer; it promotes urine and menstruation, reduces swellings, expels bladder stones, and alleviates toothache and cold stiffness.

Adhar al-Bihar: It is cold and moist, of the first degree of temperament, a small creeping plant with small branches that spread over the ground. It resembles swallow's grass. Its flower is lapis-lazuli blue like the sky. It is useful against inflammation of the road [veins], redness of the eye, and eye diseases, and repels nasal poison. It is beneficial.

Adhriyon: Well known, mostly red in color with a black center. It is useful for palpitations of the heart and excessive sweating. It is beneficial for pregnant women — if a pregnant woman takes it, she will miscarry. Some say it brings on labor for a woman in labor.

Ardamaji: Like kubrust; its smell is unpleasant. It drives away wasps and harmful insects. It is beneficial.
