Asarun: It is warm in the second degree and dry in the third degree. It removes numbness and paralysis from the limbs, promotes urination, and drives out moisture. It is found near Egypt and is beneficial.

Asras: It is warm and dry of the second degree. It drives away excess phlegm. It is beneficial.

Istarkhutas: It is warm and dry of the first and fourth degrees. It opens the three mixed thick humors, expels black bile and phlegm from the body, and is beneficial against epilepsy and melancholy.

Asqil: The mouse pear. It is warm of the third degree and dry. It is beneficial against melancholy, nerve weakness, and lethargy. It strengthens the teeth and brightens eyesight, and is beneficial against dropsy and blisters. If a fool takes it daily, it is beneficial, drives away insects, and expels wasps.

Iskandrus: It is cold and dry of the first and fourth degrees. It expels urine forcefully, strengthens the muscles, and removes joint pain.

Itrus: Its smell is foul and drives bad breath from the mouth.

It provides warmth and healing. Opium (afyimun) is warm and dry in the third degree. It drives away black bile, dissolves phlegm, opens the head; though it is harmful to the teeth and stomach. Melilot (kalil al-mulk) is warm and dry in the first degree. It softens hard swellings, strengthens the limbs, and dissolves waste matter. Amaj al-mukar is cold in the first degree and dry in the second degree, bitter in taste. It is like the skin of ants, purifies the stomach, eliminates bad odor, removes forgetfulness from the mind, settles nausea, strengthens the heart, and is suitable for those with fever. Kara is warm in the second and third degrees and dry; it increases phlegm. According to Hippocrates, it makes thick and thin humors balanced and eliminates sticky phlegm. Anise (anisun) is Roman in origin, warm and dry in the second degree. It dissolves winds, acts as an antidote to poison, opens the womb, promotes urine and menstruation, improves digestion, relieves shortness of breath. Koost al-mukar is warm and dry in the third degree; it gives strength, relieves pains, promotes urine and menstruation, and is beneficial for swellings, head pains, and heart medicines. Its fruit is called isfalabus; it is warm and dry in the second degree, promotes urine and menstruation, brings on delivery quickly, and is beneficial for epilepsy, corrupt humors, and uterine disorders. Its root is called mahmun, its gum is laxative. Karwa (caraway) is warm and dry in the third degree; it is beneficial for quartan fever, scorpion sting, consumption, tumors, and cancer. Badbakhur (coriander) — some call it kusanid — in some descriptions is warm and dry in the second degree; it freshens the breath, strengthens the stomach and

It relieves melancholy, removes palpitations, and gives warmth to the digestive system.
Parsavushan — as it is known, like Afrasiab, Siyavush, and their kin who were destroyed — this herb, when taken, restores what was lost and brings back strength like a remedy for worms.
In the first degree it is beneficial for hemorrhoids, fistulas, obstruction, and is useful for scrofula and hardened glands; it acts as a solvent. Kabuli [variety] and dry [types] relieve inflammation.
It purges phlegm and bile, cleanses the humors, and removes impurities. The cold, dry [herb] in the second degree cools heat and relieves swellings.
It benefits inflammations and winds. Burushur — cold and dry — stops bleeding of the bowels, prevents two kinds of ailments, dispels rheum and catarrh, and is beneficial for inflammations and winds.
It stops diarrhea with blood, repels two types of harm, and reduces two kinds of inflammation.
Isfayrij — warm in the second degree and dry in the third — expels bile and phlegm, opens the body, resembling narcissus and others. It resembles endive and wild celery, its fragrance removes sneezing and catarrh, carries away [impurities], and benefits sexual potency, the stomach and nerves.
Fanulus — warm in the second degree and dry in the third — expels bile, resembles giant fennel and narcissus; its fragrance removes sneezing and catarrh, benefits sexual potency, the stomach and nerves, and expels urine, menstrual blood, and hemorrhoids.
Jantaryana — its Arabic meaning is known — [illegible]

The worm dries up by the third degree; it is beneficial for the brain and dissolves the humors.
Burundan: It is a worm of the third degree; it benefits those afflicted with gout and joint ailments from cold. It is useful; Budahish: it is an antidote against all poisons.
It cures leprosy and elephantiasis. Ranas: it is better; it binds, is cold and moist.
It is beneficial for gout and swellings; the Abyssinian type is good; it provides benefit as a course for those with epilepsy.
It brings on diarrhea when used by the Sinqali people. Numush: The worm is dry, of the first degree in the fourth;
In the land of India they favor it; nine drams of it from its poison are lethal, used with weapons.
The treasures of India and all their regions are guarded by it, dwelling in the lowlands.
They use it as a herb placed under beds for children against insects, crushed and applied.
Some send it as a gift, saying it is a treasure brought from afar and stored in chests.
They send it so that with it they preserve and do not die, and through it the herb is kept.
It has the property of removing dampness, and applied as a poultice on vitiligo it removes it. The Abyssinian type drives away; Narbad: it is dry.
It is dry of the third degree; better than the Husayni type; it thickens the humors and is beneficial for
paralysis, facial palsy, leprosy, vitiligo, and nerve pains; it benefits by reducing them.
It is applied green on the skin to maintain them. Turmus (lupin): it is purifying.
It corrects; it is a worm of the first degree; the land of Halab produces it; it shows benefit.
It removes mange; applied on leprosy and on areas of skin rash it heals them.
It heals burns when applied to the affected area; mixed with vinegar it is applied. Ludraykh:
It is a worm of the second degree; moist; it increases sexual potency and thickens the humors; extracted from spikenard.
It calms and soothes. Turmon: it is a worm of the third degree; it increases urine and reduces retention.

One part of spikenard root, half a dirham per dirham of Nishapur stone — that is, what is known as "the first [stone]" — and that word, in the language of the Turks, means warm and dry in the second degree. It dissolves thick humors, promotes urination and menstruation, relieves headache, and is useful for resolving saffron-related ailments. It repels harmful creatures, resembling sarsaparilla in the first degree. In the second degree it is dry, and along with the first quality of the sea it stimulates desire, and it is warm and moderately dry. It is cold in appearance, and in the first and second degrees it disperses black bile humors, like lupine. It is warm and moist, and in the first and second degrees it disperses black bile humors. The hajj [pilgrimage] herb is drier — it peels the skin and is astringent. The melon vine produces its effect by strengthening the nerves; it is beneficial for cough, throat ailments, and pain, calms the heat, purges the body, brings luster, and tones the limbs. Khasha is warm and dry in the third degree; it preserves sight, brightens the eyes, promotes menstrual flow and urination; it expels flatulence, strengthens the power of vision, resolves the breath when it is heavy, dissolves it, and removes blemishes from the face. Dung-beetle [habbal-zibel] is warm in the second degree; theriaca and oil are beneficial; it stimulates desire and produces moisture; it is good for the stomach. Indian pepper: it is warm and dry in the third degree; it expels black bile and phlegm. Espand [wild rue] is warm in the third degree and dry in the second degree; it expels thick humors, strengthens the memory, and is beneficial. If it is burned and spread in a house, it repels harmful insects; it drives away evil and repels cold intercourse. It expels flatulence from the stomach and counteracts cold.

It is a proven remedy for bad breath and mouth sores. The dry Kūdhak is cold and dry.
In the first degree it is beneficial for wounds, sexual weakness, difficulty in urination, and colic. [It relieves] head lice.
It repels poisons and is capable; placed in the house it repels insects and other pests.
It is a warm remedy; in the second degree it relieves bad odors.
Its juice, when applied to the naranj [orange], achieves remarkable results and removes epilepsy and throat pain.
It removes hoarseness, grants benefits, promotes urination and digestion.
It corrects coldness of the stomach, relieves pain in the side, womb, and bladder when taken.
But from its vapor, if three pieces are sniffed beforehand, it clears the phlegm.
The warm and dry remedy is known in the third degree; it removes bitter taste and is well proven.
It is sought for this purpose and is placed with distilled liquids of varied colors, predominantly for digestive benefit.
It is suitable for the digestive tract, useful against dog bites and harmful creatures.
If placed in a house it drives away desert animals, livestock diseases, nervousness, and cattle ailments.
And it repels sciatica and paralysis; its root repels talismanic harms if sought.
In the second and third degree, warm and dry, it stimulates flow and promotes
urination and menstruation; one should not consume more than half a dirham at a time, otherwise harm results.
If this substance is compounded and taken in the second and third degree, dry in composition,
with half a daniq it is not broken down, and it is beneficial when mixed with ingredients for treating vertebral disorders.
Haldal-Qamar: chew its bark, and mix it with scorpion and other components.
It kills harmful insects completely; it is effective against pain. It is hot, and [known] to Seleucid medicine.
Apply it as a compress; it is effective from the first to the second degree, and it removes mange.
It appears after several days, treating scabies and skin disorders, and it relieves scales from the skin.

It benefits the body, repels fever, and expels poison; it flows from the great river.
It binds the nerves; as for the administrator, it settles him and makes him travel.
Fox: It is equivalent to a seed, of the second degree; it strengthens the loins and invigorates.
The fox: its temperament is subtly warming and useful against jaundice; in its properties it resembles the sparrowhawk.
The properties of the fox: it is like that of the raven in its strangeness, and its testicles are obedient.
The testicles of the fox — if given to a child, they make it compliant and calm phlegm.
They dissolve ulcers and scabs and drive away skin afflictions; they are known as a remedy.
Its flesh is musty-smelling and causes harm if eaten for many months and years in a row.
Its temperament is cold and moist; smeared with vinegar and applied, it is useful against jaundice.
Its urine causes difficulty in urination and difficulty in delivery; it straightens the hair.
Two mithqals of it repel vermin, and one mithqal of it relieves colic — from Ibn Sina.
It is of firm constitution; its color whitens the skin and opens the nostrils, and draws out iron.
It provokes vomiting, causes constipation; its fat softens the skin and is fattening.
Its rennet is useful; its diet of warmth and cold is tried and tested.
It withstands; truly, it is substantial and nourishing, and its nature is beneficial.
The fox: its temperament is warm and moist, and it is dry — used in treatments.
Ulcers, herpes, jaundice, and hemorrhoids — its liver is useful; hellebore.
It is dry and used in treating the stomach; it cools and aids digestion.
Gall: it is indeed their enemy; it harms worms and is drying.
It is purging, laxative, and beneficial against diarrhea; the worm is warm and dry.

The third sea: the thick winds make one ill and pains and heat from cold are present. It weakens and the warm therein is beneficial. Dilh is like mustaqī. The fourth degree: cold and dry in the fourth degree, and a complete laxative. From there the softening is drawn and cold, that is, taken from the lukewarm. It is moderate in warmth and coldness, and dry in the second degree. Dā' al-ghalab (a disease) is benefited by it, and for intestinal worms, sugar, and lāfaz and water. Bathing is harmful to it. Its essence is warm, as the noble one has called it warm; and Dīnār is dry in the third degree. Pains of the thick and smooth, and the chest breath are beneficial. It expels and causes the belly-worm to perish, and repels trembling and shivering; and zūfā is fumigated by it. Warm and moist it rubs, and terror is in its second degree and goodness. It is useful for the pain of the flank, the bladder, and what has been done, and heat is useful for it. Danbīl-hill is cold in the first degree and dry in the second. It expels flatulence, menstrual flow, and urinary suppression without weakness. Epistaxis in the head: warm and fearful it comes, and four kernels broken with water, and it is cold and moist. Dāl: cold and dry in the second degree. It gives strength to sa'd, and resembles warmth. Ḥurnuq: it grows like cucumber, warm and dry in the first degree. It benefits vitiligo, psoriasis, and mange. Its smell drives away reptiles and insects. From al-Jawzī it is said that the yellow mongoose gives it, and it habitually regulates the temperament. The pains it resembles: sores of the mucous membranes, and it repels the diseases thereof. Silk (thread-worm) is benefited by it.

Duqa (a plant/worm): It is warm and dry; it benefits the liver, and it is easy-acting; it benefits the stomach and the organs, relieves pain, and calms the limbs. It is beneficial for catarrh and thickens mucus. It makes thick humors subtle, warms the limbs. It is useful for the bath; it is warm in the first degree and dry; it benefits the complexion and is useful for discharges and phlegmatic conditions. It is useful for hemorrhoids.

Zarawand (Aristolochia): It warms and dries and removes thick winds, opens obstructions, and is useful for wounds and ulcers. It relieves colic, spleen pain, and flank pain. It is beneficial for tumors.

Zarnabad (a plant): It is warm and dry; it expels winds and repels harmful creatures. It drives away cold and humid vapors.

Zanjabil (Ginger): It is warm and dry; it digests phlegm, removes it from the intestines and stomach, drives out winds from the stomach, and is useful for digestion.

Narigi (a citrus): Its quality is that it repels cold and humid substances.

Sajam: It is warm in the first degree and temperate in the second; placed in water it strengthens the stomach, promotes urination, and in the middle of the sea it protects against harm.

Hinduba (chicory) makes the mouth pleasant and gives delight to the heart. Suranjan (colchicum) is cold in nature.
It expels waste matter, removes impurities, but is harmful to the stomach. Saatar (thyme):
It also sought out the key, and the worms it kills and dries.
In the third degree it expels wind and phlegm, purifies the bile, and promotes urination.
It relieves constipation, strengthens vision, relieves headache, and aids digestion.
It kills intestinal worms, is beneficial for those bitten by serpents, and is like spinach. Sa'd (a plant):
In the second degree it is useful for difficult urination, expels stones,
is beneficial for the bowels, expels wind, relieves colic, and settles the stomach.
Samarniya: it is praiseworthy, kills worms, and dries the excess.
In the third degree it expels bile and phlegm, but is harmful to the stomach; it is corrected with vinegar.
It diminishes appetite for food; vinegar mixed with it acts as an astringent. Halil (myrobalan):
Sabestan is cold and moist in the second degree; it regulates the temperament of the bowels.
It is beneficial for toothache. Sana Makki (Indian senna): its pods are used and it is beneficial.
It was sent from the Prophet, peace be upon him, as a cure and a remedy against death.
Sana (senna): its root is used and it is warm; it purifies corrupt humors.
It weakens the ill and removes foul odor; it is beneficial and purges. Shahterj (fumitory): it is soothing.
It is beneficial in clearing the blood, warm, in the first degree, and is known and tested.
Its taste is slightly bitter, its character is wise; it is beneficial for urination and slightly loosens.
Shaqaqul (field carrot): warm in the third degree, slightly moistening, beneficial for virility.
It is moderately beneficial in the second degree, slightly sweet and moist, balanced in temperament.
It benefits virility and the heart. Shaqatul Mughan: Ibn Lala described its characteristics and uses in the cities.

It belongs to the second liver; its skin removes worms and is dry. Henna removes ulcers and eruptions and clears the bile. Apply it with snake-grass to stimulate urine and menstruation; its juice is beneficial. It relieves stomach pain and eye inflammation, and cools it; lentil-water made from it is used. White Sanjār — some say it is among the choicest remedies — resembles lettuce; it breaks wind and its stalks, finely ground, benefit the finger-joints. Applied as a poultice it eliminates harm, and when a pregnant woman uses it the cramps are relieved. Applied under silver it is beneficial for announcing good tidings. Hemlock (Shawkarān) is cold; it harms the fourth liver and weakens digestion, numbering among those that paralyze the legs like cucumber. It resembles anise, is entirely white, and is among the resins. Shalīrāj — the best of it is taken medicinally — removes worms from the third liver and clears spots. It reveals the decline of the body through application; unripe aloe (ṣabr) is excellent. It is harmful to the first liver and weakens digestion and thirst; in the end it weakens the vision; the unripe variety is among those harmful to the stomach; it strengthens the organs. It purifies the blood, eliminates harmful bile and phlegm from the organs, and when taken with the rectum it is not harmful. Ṭarāmalat is beneficial. It is a cold plant, harmful to the second liver and weak in digestion for the third liver; it strengthens the limbs and eliminates blood from the belly. Ṭarīfān is like safflower and is among the yellow dyes and is used as a poultice. It is placed to relieve toothache and brings on menstruation. Sangār removes worms and is dry. It is useful for the first liver; vipers' bugloss clears ulcers and is beneficial for swellings. It is harmful to the first liver, weak in the second digestion, smooth and slippery for the organs, and is useful for hemorrhages. Shināra — apply it like fish — kills worms.

And its harm is like badaq, and one dirham of its side is three grains; it is a laxative, and it is made into flour. It is excellent, and dry in the first degree, and in the fourth compound — that is, from the class of royal plants. It is beneficial for joint pains, gout, dropsy, and sciatica.
It sharpens the senses and relieves colic; it prevents tooth decay and strengthens the humors, and is two drams in weight; it is known from dahliaash. It is said that it nourishes and fattens, and it is of various kinds. It is good for the blood, and for the semen and toothache. It is emetic; it is combined with zarqatalist — this is the Mary's Tree. Its astringent property is noted; its root causes sneezing; it destroys lice and worms. It relieves pain from the womb, and drives away the falling sickness, scrofula, and heals them; it is beneficial. Tarragon: it is like meat, it firms loose teeth and relieves trembling. Asparagus: some barbers administer it; it calms children when crushed. Its juice when prepared removes mouth pain and silences it. Grape of the fox (Solanum): it is of three types: cultivated, wild, and eight-seeded. Four are known to be nutritious; it brings on sleep; and its root is called jamnafal. From these five types it gives benefit. Squill: its root, taken in the morning, and its properties: it opens, purifies, and cures madness, epilepsy, dropsy, insanity, and kidney stones; it strengthens the womb and is beneficial for sciatica and nerve pain. Camphor: it reduces fever and is repeatedly beneficial; it is the root of the archer-plant. In the third degree it heals the stomach, stops burning sensations, arrests bleeding, and suppresses desire. It brings down high blood and reduces it. Ivy: [continues].

It resembles the strength [of a plant] and its leaves are from the cold tree; it is cold, in the second degree.
The third: it repels phlegm, is beneficial for the intestines, strengthens the stomach, stops nosebleeds.
It is beneficial. In the end, it is warm in the first degree of phlegm, and dry; it nourishes.
It gives [benefit]. Farnahan is cold and rough; it heals sores, removes blackness of the teeth, and is cooling.
It extinguishes burning sensation. Fartajmashk is warm and dry in the second degree.
It opens the brain, relieves palpitations; its black smoke and vapors [give benefit].
Qust is warm and dry in the first degree; together they resist [ailments].
That is to say, it is recognized as warm and dry in the second degree.
Sabirza Asafidast Finjangat is warm in the fourth degree and dry.
It resembles the brushwood of Zabon; its use is recommended for washing and cleaning the hair.
It cleans the color of the skin, relieves headache, and is useful against worms and vermin.
It is beneficial for phlegm and the body, and it expels worms.
It is warm in the first degree and dry in the second; it promotes urine and digestion.
It gives benefit. Amir-Aqu is warm and dry in the first degree.
Red [variety] is beneficial; it removes jaundice, trembling, and relieves itching.
It is useful; it purges yellow bile and phlegm. Fasiru is warm and dry.
Together they resist [ailments]. Qatli is not recognized as warm and dry.
In the first degree it promotes urination and semen, and purges yellow bile. Qasha Ra Al-Juhar
is warm and dry in the second degree; Habaqa brings strength and removes [ailments].
Its extract is used for children's illness, in jaundice, and for chronic headache, and clears it.
Four [physicians] have indicated it; Qabil is warm and dry in the second degree.

It is beneficial and expels long worms. The moon [qar]: it is dry and cold in the second degree of Hajjar, and brings forth fresh [matter]; it is harmful to epilepsy but beneficial for the intestines. It is dry and cold in the second degree of Hajjar; its second property draws out [substances] from the teeth and gums, and opens the liver; it removes vitiligo, skin disease, and bad odor. It is cold in its nature and is beneficial in the third degree; it opens urination and menstruation, opens the abdomen and intestines, and is beneficial for a cold womb. "Qurd mata" — it repels [harm]. In the third degree it resists deadly poisons and repels scrofula if applied, and if a woman takes it, it expels the fetus, and if vermin bite, Qiṭrūn drives them away. It thickens [humors] and settles them; it is dry and cold in the second degree of Hajjar; it expels [matter] and if placed in the womb it stops bleeding that has come forth, and [relieves] dryness of the muscles, tightness of breath, and chronic cough. Qiṭrūn, in terms of rank, is warm and dry; its branches, leaves, and blossoms are used in twenty ways; it opens sciatica and hardness of the spleen. "Faṭūm" — it has been said that it is known to snakes, because snakes [seek it since] it warms and dries their bodies. In the second degree it strengthens the power of the stomach and heart, increases eyesight, promotes urination, brings on appetite, nourishes the body, treats vitiligo, promotes hair growth for animals; and "Āl-pūl" — its water repels poison; place it in a cup with wine. It is cold and dry in the fourth degree of Hajjar, and preserves the mind. Qurṭ — it is cold; it is cold in the first degree of Rajab. Its properties in the second: fresh [use] warms and [its] dry [use] cools, and its properties strengthen.

It benefits the stomach; its extract is cold. It is of the second degree. Its nature is such that it is useful for enemas with the intestines, and for drinking it is beneficial, and for bringing out what is in the stomach it is useful. [Karm kanak:] It removes mange and itching, whitening of the nails, and is a remedy for gum disease. It brings on sneezing, removes nightmare, and its smell corrects [conditions]. It can be obtained easily. [Kah:] Well known; it is cold, of the second degree. It grows under the earth by the influence of the moon, like truffles and mushrooms. Its excessive use causes paralysis, stroke, facial palsy, and colic. It crumbles stones and gravel, and from it also relieves toothache. From the Prophet, peace be upon him: "Truffle water heals colic, difficulty of urination," and likewise he said: "The extract of truffle is from the manna, and its water heals eye ailments." [Karzabol:] Warm and dry, of the second degree. It removes thick humors, repels the poison of reptiles, and is a laxative. [Kati:] It is warm and dry, of the second degree; a diuretic; it quenches thirst; it treats hemorrhoids and bleeding. [Lablāb:] Some Persians call it sanubaza and barat qu. Warm and dry; it benefits chronic conditions of the spleen; expels bile. [Its ash is] useful for scorching the hair, and killing lice and swellings. It is cold; it strengthens the stomach; it expels cold materials; its extract benefits the patients of various illnesses and [guards against] poisonous things.

The ox-tongue plant: its root is warm and of the first degree, strengthening the heart and bringing joy; it prevents inflammation; drinking it in moderation increases vitality and cheerfulness. The borage plant is cold and dry, of the first degree; it purifies and removes putrid humors, eliminates fistulas and chronic ailments, restores lost functions, and is beneficial for healing.

The wild herb described is of the second degree, useful for vitiligo, deafness, and certain skin conditions. It is known among herbalists that it calms both males and females, soothes agitation of the limbs, and brings peace to the heart.

The root of the wild lufah plant is extremely cold in temperament; if taken as a decoction in drink, it induces sleep and quenches thirst. If a suppository is made from it with water and oil, it acts powerfully and its effects are strong upon the body.

The Mamunch worm is dry, of the second degree; dissolved in water and applied, it causes weakness in the joints and relieves forgetfulness; it stabilizes the mind.

Andrion: it is warm and of various types; it is warm and dry, of the fourth degree. Its seeds and husks are bound together; it blackens and its seeds and husks, two dirhams each, are useful for all types of blemishes, ringworm, skin discoloration, scrofula, and conditions of moisture. It is among the best medicines.

Mamna: cold and dry, of the first degree, and among its properties...

[Marginalia:] Scales of the tongue [or: fish scales of the tongue — فلوس اژنان]

It corrects errors, and the eye-salve (shiyaf) of mamishan is useful for most ailments. Myrtle (murd) is dry; it breaks the second degree of stones, closes off the canals, and expels intestinal worms.
And electuary (amlaj) strengthens the stomach's power and gives nourishment; and when old women use it as a suppository, it is beneficial.
One dang of it, taken as an enema, expels thick winds, is useful for the intestines, and stops bleeding from the mouth.
When it is applied as a plaster, it is necessary to mix it with oils; it is useful for the people of Khurasan, for cleaning and irrigating wounds, binding hemorrhages, removing dental plaque and decay.
It stops bleeding of wounds, is beneficial for wounds and injuries, expels pain from the gums.
It promotes urination; maru (marjoram), maru — it is dry in the third degree; it is useful for coldness of the womb
And pains of the womb and joints are treated by it; it provokes sneezing and headaches.
It is useful for the stomach in the second degree, and in the third degree it is hot; it benefits digestion and relieves hiccups; when drunk it is beneficial.
Smoke from it produces beneficial effects. Lavender (usqrum) — dry and hot:
It is useful for brain ailments in the first degree and benefits sugar patients; it is moist.
It is dry in the second degree; it nourishes, relieves gargling and phlegm.
When used externally, it cools the heat, and with honey water it benefits
It is useful in the third degree; it is dry and reduces stomach ailments.
Nettles (nish): they are known as a plant with toxicity; for this reason, contact with nettles is not without risk.
It is not free from astringency. Cloves (karanful) — dry in the third degree; they are hot.
They are beneficial and produce warmth; they strengthen hearing.
They are good for the stomach; they promote urination and digestion; worm is dry and hot in the third degree.
And these humors are well-dispersed by it, and it promotes urination and softens hardness.

It repels [harm] and its vapors bring relief to the chest, and is beneficial for pain in the side and chest.
Sitting [in it] relieves the pain of red bile. Hormuzjan: it is warm and dry, of the second degree.
It increases breathing difficulties, thickens the humors, and relieves itching through its nature.
It is beneficial and helps expel corrupted waste matter from the body through gradual action.
The plant known as Tarul is among the best of its kind, white and large.
It is a fine plant that is well-known, found among dung-heaps in the middle ground.
It is gathered from the earth in spring, stripped of its bark, resembling carob, and taken away.
Its properties should be recognized and noted; one should not wish to exceed its use.
No more than two mithqals should be consumed, nor should it be applied as a poultice excessively.
Place beside it some Birjis to increase moisture and to settle the temperament.
If it is soaked and the water is drunk, it will not harm and will not cause dryness.
Fresh: it warms and moistens. Hal: it is moderately warm and dry in the second degree.
It aids digestion of food and strengthens it. Khamish: warm and dry.
It is useful in the third degree, repels flatulence, relieves constipation, and is beneficial.
It warms the body, clears the intestines, and expels gases from the stomach. There are seven
varieties: one of them is from a tree, saffron-colored, and known as Nusalun.
Halendan: it heals sores, fistulas, and ulcers, and is beneficial for healing.
It nourishes and when taken regularly, it softens the body, removes bad odor.
If four drops of its juice are placed in [the ear or nose], it heals and clears it.
When dried it is astringent. Soaked, with its gum dissolved, it repels poisons and toxins.
It has a pleasant fragrance. Among its properties: it is brought from those lands, and its fragrances are well known.

Chapter: It is known that these matters are established, even if their benefits are mostly external. It is not appropriate to write them merely in letters, but it was deemed more fitting to record them thus — and so we write these letters: it is reported that it is among the finest and most pleasing things.

No fragrance is more excellent for improving the condition of the mouth, treating eye inflammation (ramad), and strengthening the heart.

Afus (a plant substance) is warm in the first degree, useful for killing worms, drying excess moisture, and benefiting those suffering from pain in the joints. It protects against harm and, by the power of the Almighty and the Most Compeller, is known to benefit learning and judgment and is reported as a companion and peer.

The third degree: its white and red varieties are suitable. That is, it is entirely beneficial for the bladder and urinary passages, though excessive use is harmful.

It is cold and moist in the first degree; it benefits headaches, hair, and the throat and is useful for scabies, conditions of the mouth and passages, and produces refinement.

Kharaghan: its form resembles spikenard; it grows in shrubs and its origin is from spikenard, somewhat more open in form, and in its properties it resembles spikenard.

Henna: it is cold and dry in the first degree. Burnt henna dropped into the mouth is reported to be beneficial. Two parts of henna moistens and soothes dry conditions. Its flowers are beneficial — henna is temperate in warmth and coldness, moderately drying. It benefits the gums, relieves pain, and is useful for the mouth.

The third kind — yellow, red, and white — refreshes the brain, purifies the thick winds, and removes what settles on the surface in recurring fashion. It relieves fainting, scabies, and the pain of pleurisy, and brings benefit. It gives strength in the preparation of remedies, as is known from the physicians of Jesus. It is beneficial for the offspring and for faintness, as the order is given — known as "duwalm." Iran and Makan: sipa is placed gently upon the face, in the manner that replaces the qallaq. It brings joy, and is known as a plant — sāsfarum — the ryhan (basil) of the Arabs, jandal, small in kind, from the pomegranate regions. Each body is larger; it diminishes the young, and in the era of Nushirwan, Sipdashrm is known, and Sha-Safar is praised with melody and tune. The city of Jabra: the first is of two layers of stone, suited for marrow, and brings warmth, and is known as saffron — sipa rāja piya — and it is thus. It is good for bites, flatulence, and from the tree of Jesus, and from the mountain-root it strengthens and sustains. The whitish kind is of moderate temperament, and the second is dry, with a measure of increase and refinement, bringing forth food and purging, giving pleasure, and bringing laughter. And it is more than jnqal — its root is the onion — and is beneficial. Saffron nourishes and is given as food to the pale and the colored, and is used as fuel. It is in the highest degree soft and fine, soothes the troubled mind, and is well-suited — sadab (rue) altogether. It is fragrant, spread with oil and rubbed; sipa contains it. Especially for things arising from cold, it is known as warm and dry. The third kind promotes urination, refines the humors, and removes superfluities, bringing them out.

And they fed Balaam, and it was not compatible, and the smell repelled vermin and drove them away. Its juice was sought for rubbing on women's bodies, and the smoke of it was burned to repel partridges and gnats, and to overcome fatigue and numbness.
And it was used for joints, by way of consuming it by mouth with strength, and it is beneficial to eliminate worms and dryness, and to settle the four humors.
The resin called "Salab" was known to soften dryness and break it up and repel vermin, and it causes movement and softening and dispels [ailments].
SUMBUL [Nard/Spikenard]: It is well known, warm and dry in the second degree, and it is good for breaking [illness].
This plant is recognized as similar to nard in its fragrance and has been called "Layth." It does not fail. The Greeks knew of it and its scent enters the brain strongly and after that it strengthens it. It drives away palpitations, increases urine, dispels phlegm, and Indian spikenard is close to it in this.
SUSAN [Lily]: It is well known, warm and dry in the second degree, of good scent. It causes sleep and drives away vermin from the air, and relieves headache, mange, and pain in nerves, difficulty of urination, and fever. It is beneficial for winds. Its oil is used to relieve difficulty in childbirth, and repels foul odors, and relieves pain in the mouth. The root of the lily, when crushed and the thick mixture of it placed on the chest, relieves it and stops diarrhea. It is warm and dry in the second degree, and repels vermin.
SURA [another plant]: It relieves rheumatism and joint pain and is beneficial like almonds, and thickens thick [phlegm]. It is well known. And thus, all of them were sought: warm and dry they break [illness] in the second degree.
SISAN [another plant]: They rub it on the limbs for benefit, and it grows among vermin and drives them away, and its fruit...

The body it carries away forgetfulness, and separates what is foundational, and revives the dead, and brings down [certain things], and removes semen, and induces menstruation, and crushes [kidney stones].

The fourth branch: its interior and bark repel [diseases], and it resembles [certain remedies] that reduce worms.

Its poultice treats skin eruptions and repels [the disease known as] ata al-ghalab, and relieves pain and swelling.

It is beneficial: fenugreek [farkh] removes [obstructions], treats kohl-like [eye conditions], and its bark is good for relieving [ailments].

Its smoke repels harmful creatures; if one drinks its juice it benefits cupping and skin sores, relieves intestinal worms, cough, shortness of breath, jaundice, dropsy, and restores the body.

"Fil kush" [Elephant's ear]: in Arabic it is called [this name] for it resembles [an elephant's ear]. It heals wounds quickly and together with honey it colors [things] with various hues.

It is also called marzangush [marjoram]; it is also known as hinna al-nil and anbar. It treats hardness of the spleen, dropsy, facial paralysis, difficulty urinating, and [relieves] menstruation, expels flatulence.

The second stone: first [used with] mortar, it promotes urination, relieves nasal congestion, and induces menstruation. Nardeen [spikenard]:

The second [use]: the first and third [preparations] from it are astringent. It treats leg [conditions], total paralysis, facial paralysis, urinary retention, and menstruation.

It is beneficial for digestion and stomach [ailments]; sprinkled [in food] it benefits [the person]. For example, narcissus [narjis]: consume [it] — it reduces worms and is good as a first [remedy].

This is reported from the Prophet, peace be upon him: the best of perfumes is musk. Hold it close [to use] for the chest and heart. Squill and colocynth and cupping — there is no cure for them except in these names of [remedies].

It nourishes and even in a general sense it is regarded as nourishment for the spirit, and it is included among the creatures of wonder. It is said that narcissus, when taken along with other roots and given to a woman for seven days in succession, is beneficial. If four dirhams of narcissus are given with sal ammoniac to a woman who cannot conceive, it helps her to become pregnant. Its scent is cooling and soothing, and it is close to moderation in the first degree. If placed in water and boiled, and the steam inhaled, it relieves headache, joint pain, and flatulence. When thrown into fire it burns and raises bubbles, and it relieves headache and skin conditions. However, it reduces the appetite and is dry and diminishing in nutrition. In the second degree it is useful for cold pains of the nerves and for thick flatulence. The water-lily: its scent is pleasant. The water-lily draws water upward. It has the property that each plant which it encounters it suppresses. Its nutritional and medicinal value is limited, but it is not without its purposes and benefits. It is better to understand its properties by learning its names. Let us mention the names: in Greek it is a certain plant resembling a human figure, male and female. The male strengthens and the female arouses desire for intercourse, and if one drinks it in wine it has a powerful effect, and it is reported that those who use it in the land of Tabaristan know this. Glasswort: it is warm and dry. In the second degree it is green, yellow, and white. A small amount of it promotes the flow of urine and menstruation. Six dirhams of it given to a child can cause abortion, and ten dirhams is lethal. Its smoke kills insects. The rest of the particulars that are sought are that it is warm and dry, and after it comes the poison.

The uses and properties of kureish are beneficial, and when applied as a poultice they bring great benefit.
Among its properties: rubbing with coriander relieves pain; some Arabs call it "nashnapha."
Those who sought the herb found it to be a worm-repellent and drying agent; it has no particular taste but may be used.
When consumed regularly, it strengthens the constitution, extinguishes fever, promotes urination and menstruation.
Its roots are beneficial; its head is a plant called "shar," and it protects against blights of vegetation.
Wherever it grows, it quickly covers the ground, its branches spreading and shading the earth.
The first use: it heals fresh wounds and expels kidney stones.
It is well known that smoke from it is also named "bastan" in coastal regions.
It is called "khurwa" — which the Persians call "bachak" — it relieves pain and lassitude.
It is cold; one should use it carefully in repeated treatments each year.
Over several years it is beneficial and reduces fatty deposits on the body.
Two handfuls applied to the head with camphor, ground finely, act like an alkali.
Every herb of this kind repels worms and helps the teeth; it is the third degree of warmth.
When mixed with vinegar it is used for the skin; it produces effects like the "jawbulana" and "lawdabira."
As mentioned in "Wonders of Creation": when consumed at the time of encounter,
facial pain and enemy harm cease; apply water to the scalp to relieve it.
Filtering and purifying strengthens the joints, relieves pain in the knees and ankles.
"Runas" (madder) is well known: cold and dry in temperament, and its green form is beneficial.
It promotes urination and menstruation, and its dry red form expels phlegm.
Four parts mixed together, taken daily, with two portions of meat consumed, build great muscle.
The plant "nil" (indigo) is warm and dry; used in the second degree, it removes spots, vitiligo, and heart palpitations.

Wounds and ulcers are benefited by it; among the rare useful things, eating gold is reported to be beneficial. The water of this plant is smooth, intoxicating, and expels worms.
Second: when dry, as it was when fresh, it acts as a clarifier; it is derived from Abrias.
And the one afflicted with facial paralysis (laqwa) will find benefit and it will increase his understanding. Cotton: it is said to be beneficial in warming the body, and it increases knowledge and intelligence. It is used in treating wounds initially; it is applied several times until healing occurs, and the infection is expelled.
It is said that it opens the first layer; when dry, the putrefaction is like its natural temperament.
Applying it to wounds is beneficial, and minium (red lead): grinding it well is a great remedy.
They grind it and grind it finely; the plant is a good remedy, but one must be cautious, for it is dangerous in Khurasan.
It is reported that it is equal for women and counteracts the excessive growth of flesh. Third level, earthly.

Discussion of Animals: By the wisdom of God Almighty, the creation of animals was ordained by God the Exalted.
He decreed that all of them, derived from His grace, and that through the original principle His traces would be established. The horse
is a means of comfort and enrichment for humanity in every manner; its mention and existence
were given by God the Exalted to humanity, who named it and described it.
Dogs and horses were given beauty, movement and grace so that putrefaction
would be removed from the body through their movement; by this means, the putrefaction of the human body
is expelled from the person, and some of it causes flatulence, and some of it is dispersed.
Human movement increases, and at the time of need, humanity does not require further exertion.
The soul, by its own nature, attracts benefit and repels harm — this the wise person understands.

Survival

It sustains and is the source: whoever gives of everything what it requires, without excess or deficiency, the prince endures. And since in our time, for the sake of mankind, from some wisdom the Lord created the world in good order, He did not withhold benefit, so that the nature of the sons of Adam would lack no good. They serve as mounts and as food and tillage, as God the Exalted has said: "We have created these things for them," meaning We have made them subservient to them — some for riding and some for eating. And the meaning is that He gave them the faculty of instruction: had they not possessed the nature of obedience, they would not have been tamed through training; yet some were domesticated and some were broken. And certain ones, through familiarity, were guided so that they could be led by the hand, and their full excellence was realized — hence the saying about them. And none knows what lies hidden in plants except Him. Yet they have become known to us through experience: if a land animal or sea animal encounters and rubs against ambergris, and any creature licks it with hand or paw, and any bee comes out of the hive flying, and every source of honey flows out — these are all signs. And wherever there are branches, the flies gather on them, [and they indicate good things]. As for the lawful and unlawful: however many are called by that name for any reason, it was reported after the Prophet — peace be upon him — that the Messenger of God declared forbidden every fanged beast of prey and every taloned bird. These are the established points of benefit.

FIRST SECTION: On the mention of animals — land animals, birds, and insects — mentioning domestic animals with their characteristics, in ten qualities, arranged alphabetically. We shall mention the camel: it is called in Persian "ushtur," in Arabic "jamal," and a she-camel is "nāqa," a young one "bikr," a male "fahl," and various other names. The one swift in pace is called "nājiya," and an excellent camel "najīb," and the young camel not yet two years old is called "ibl."

A horse at three years is called "rāhiq," at four years "rabī'," at five years "mukhtālif ghazal," at six years "khalfa," at seven years "unthā," at eight years "bārbāyī," at nine years "sadlabas," at nine years "bādhil," at ten years "mukhtālif," and its foal is called "khawār." The term for a beast of burden is "al-hawl," and nursing mares are called "nātij." Mares that have not been bred are called "iskān" and "kanzat." Among the Arabs of the open desert, such terms exist and their use is widespread. The camel's form is large and its neck tall, and it is patient. "Do they not look at the camels, how they are created?" — a verse about the desert Arabs. The camel is an animal counted among the lawful (halal) to eat; its dried and fresh meat is good food, though it produces black bile and is heavy on the stomach. Its milk is profitable, as it purges the belly, expels kidney stones and eye ailments. Its urine treats urinary incontinence. Its various uses include carrying loads and providing wool. The mule is born between a horse and a donkey. It is more durable than a horse and is less distressed by hardship. Its uses include carrying heavy loads and traveling over difficult terrain. Among domestic animals it is one of the rarest in reproduction because of limited mating capacity; a mature mule cannot breed with another of its kind, nor produce offspring with a horse or donkey.

It has no festival measure, its breaking and exit is in the jamal star and Sa'd — it is auspicious. And if living things are brought in at the time when the crescent moon has not yet appeared, it is beneficial, because the lawful outweighs the unlawful, and consuming what derives from the unlawful is also unlawful.

If a donkey, a horse, a deputy, and a domestic animal are among those lawfully slaughtered — but there is a rare ruling that one may give, and from a rare ruling it is judged forbidden — the heart of the rider...

If one feeds horse dung to a person, and it is used in the manner of a remedy for mares, it will cause the hair of mice to grow. If a pregnant woman places the dried remains on her arm and body, it will cause her to miscarry. If a pregnant woman carries it, it is harmful. The Arabs call it baqar nafri.

Its gathering and assembly causes benefit to pass away, and eating the flesh is permissible.

The dung of the grazing beast is lawful; consuming it increases health, and at the proper time it increases the flow. If it is placed among the flock that grazes the meadow, and when it is rubbed on the foot like a green poultice, it restores health from sunrise, and its poison repels harm.

If it is gently applied and rubbed with a little powder on the shoulder as a poultice of gold, it is beneficial. If made into a morning preparation with a little remedy given at once, it alleviates the condition. Mixed with honey it treats throat inflammation; its nature is cold and dry, and it diminishes appetite. It induces coldness, causes dryness, and tightens the flesh.

Its meat is free of harm to the degree it is consumed, and no disease is absent from it. Among its properties are that it treats cancer, plague, leprosy, and brings forth from the Nile a remedy for tumors and qualities that last for years.

It renders one generous; it increases sexual potency and sharpens the sense of smell. It creates enmity between two people. Its flour mixed with crow's [dung] and applied as a poultice cures hemorrhoids. Henna applied as a plaster is beneficial; its first application mixed with certain things purifies the hands and feet. It binds garlic; a quarter of asafoetida mixed with dung of [certain animals], cool in nature, aids difficult childbirth and facilitates delivery. Rubbing its dung on sesame-based preparations is healing — this is called hawsh — and it settles the stomach. Applied to the skin with the peel of certain fruits it removes brain-worms and is useful against intestinal worms. It reduces sleep when eaten as food, causes flatulence, is mostly slow to digest, and generally overcomes other foods when combined. The one who eats it regularly will have a sharp mind, good sleep, and a refined intellect. It removes freckles, vitiligo, and scabies; when burned and inhaled as fumigation it is effective. It is called by the people ramafan; it is hot in temperament and is known among the Arabs as al-humr. When ground and rubbed on, mixed with certain warming things, it is most beneficial. It is extremely cold in its natural temperament and eating it is forbidden. Among its properties: it settles the stomach, relieves colic, and when taken with its kernel and with certain plant extracts it removes unwanted hair and sharpens the mind. It induces sleep, suppresses [certain ailments], and purifies the blood. It benefits vitiligo and skin eruptions when combined with henna applied to the joints and affected areas. When eaten it corrects ulcers and sores and brings about healing. Fresh dung of it, when applied to the gums, stops bleeding; rubbing it on certain parts gathers dispersed hemorrhoidal matter and relieves the condition. The bilious person benefits from its use and it aids digestion.

In the margin: [dar murab — "in the margin/note"]

They put it in the mouth; Arab physicians use it gargled hot to relieve toothache.
When it is used as a snuff, it removes mucus from the nose; it is like milk in some of its properties.
Its benefits are that it helps digestion, aids recovery, and is useful for those suffering from certain conditions.
It is mentioned in four places; it is called the Great Sour [garlic/onion]; the Arabs, Turks,
Persians, and Mongols all eat it, though it is considered reprehensible in time of worship, and eating it is forbidden
and prohibited at the time of anger, for one loses one's senses in rage.
For this reason, wise physicians advise that it should be used carefully, as it may cause imbalance
in the body and have adverse effects; it is mentioned in the Mujmal al-Lugha.
It is said that large amounts mixed with poison of scorpion, if given at night, sharpen
the mind; and if mixed together, it is beneficial for those suffering from paralysis.
It is useful for the spleen; pounded and applied to wounds, it promotes healing; the black variety bandages
and stops bleeding; it prevents excessive flow of blood.
Leprosy patients: it is said it is not beneficial for them; it is used as a poultice for gout and helps the residents
if applied; if one applies it, it separates adhesions and dries the skin.
And if applied with bandages to wounds and injuries, it draws out excess moisture from sheep.
The leaders requested and they permitted it in Ramadan, and it is permitted for the people and horses —
it is lawful; the Prophet, peace be upon him, said in a hadith: "The sheep is a blessing."
One dirham per year increases and grows; it is sometimes used by people sparingly.
By comparison it is well-known; it removes poisons and the basis of sweets.
It is prescribed in dirhams per year; people from those lands eat none of it,
and their numbers diminish; their tails decrease; the wisdom behind their numbers is preservation.

God is gentle and compassionate toward His servants; He is capable of all things. Regarding livestock and property:
The sheep in this form is mentioned — and when it makes a sound, it drives away fear, as the Quran states.
Its properties: it is beneficial; mix its fat with honey and apply it — it clears the eye and relieves eye ailments.
If the evil eye is treated with it, it takes away the mark; whoever carries it, it protects.
It has many benefits. The meat of a young sheep is wholesome; eating mutton is good.
Praising God, eating it in moderation — the meat of an old animal, if one is not careful, can be harmful.
Sheep's [milk and products] are most often beneficial; yogurt, cheese, cotton, and dried curds
are prepared from them; each has its well-known properties listed here in the Book of Wonders.
The blessing of wealth spreads; it was known for seven [properties].
Because it was brought from Hind [India], the meat is excellent.
Two by two, in the manner of sheep, and there it was first renewed.
In Fars [Persia], the white [sheep] became very numerous; the sheep's meat
is abundant there. In this region the sheep
that gives birth twice — its meat, if it is a twice-birthing sheep,
is good. As for the horse — [Arabic:] "And prepare against them whatever force you can, including the tying of horses, to terrify thereby the enemy of God and your enemy" [Quran 8:60].
The horse is noble and great; God is forgiving and pardoning to the free.
"And prepare against them whatever strength you are able, including steeds of war" — to terrify thereby the enemy of God and the enemy of His Messenger.
The horse's goodness is tied to its forelock until the Day of Resurrection; it brings reward.
Its gait, its run, its training and care — eating its meat: according to the Shafi'i school it is permissible; according to Maliki and some others it is disapproved.

When one burns aloe-wood incense it induces sleep; rubbing the head with rock candy removes the headache; it purges the body and enables intercourse; if applied to freckles and blemishes on the skin it heals them; it relieves colic of the joints and gout; mixing wax and applying it to the site of a spasm brings relief; it stops the trembling of limbs and relieves pain in the teeth and pain in the back.

Whoever offers five presents will receive camels — the mountain goat is known among the Turks, the Mongols, the Arabs, and others; among all schools of law its flesh is considered lawful; every year it sheds its horns; it drives away enemies and scorpions; its flesh roasted with a misqal of sugar taken on an empty stomach benefits epileptics; rubbed on, it treats vitiligo and leucoderma; its fat relieves hemorrhoids; its smoke repels snakes, worms, and insects; it possesses a special quality against the gallbladder; ground and mixed with sesame it is good medicine.

The mountain goat's blood, when burned and mixed with hot water and applied as a plaster, prevents the sting of scorpions and bees; it is beneficial for the generative faculty; its roasted flesh gives sexual potency; its skin is well known.

The fox (tha'lab): there are two opinions — according to the Shafi'i school it is lawful, and according to Abu Hanifa it is forbidden; it is an animal well known in various lands; if one eats its meat and drinks a decoction made of it, it removes cataract from the eye; its flesh is used in cooking and eaten.

The loquat is beneficial; a person lets out a cry, and if it is rubbed with pomegranate wood, the feet come together and the mind is gathered. Kalim-shad, the mouth of the khinar returned; they bind the testicles around the neck of the kuk; it prevents affliction. It comes forth, and the fish-like creature of the deep sea, in its middle, remains; with ink and inscription it is kept outside. It achieves its purpose by crushing its worm-like parts, straightening them, and preventing adultery.

Al-wasr and the desired thing are established — in the book of Nashikh it is said to mean that the branches of Khusraw's head are wealth, and it is said that the animals settle there, and the wealth is such that within its shadow all qualities are present. A young person, through certain of its properties, does not harm anyone, and when it is heard, the pig's cub, the khanzir, the animal Rasib, a living being stands firm and its own destruction it causes; the sparrow flies away and the female is driven from the nest.

Al-Nasr-tanz is a remedy altogether, and it is not among the living animals that do not know and are not pleasant. It is accepted that the foal is brought forth; the people of Persia say the female goes inside, and by its feathers it scratches from desire. And by its special properties and eating of it, it does not grant desire and is used as remedy; it enters the forest seeking cure, and in the wilderness of creation it brings forth.

The karakul/sifah cools the body, and the wild ass removes and enters the inside. The pig compared to the elephant is clear: its urine benefits hemorrhoids, and its bristles are useful — placed upon the skin they bring benefit. Al-Uwais grants soundness and by its fat rubbed upon it, gold is applied and health is given to the joints. If it is bound around something and placed in the middle, no harm from afflictions will reach it, and if it is hung, when it becomes white like a ball it goes away, and if in [illegible] —

The second stone: A horse has a pleasing appearance, is well-bred in color, gentle among animals, and they appreciate each other's goodness. With good appearance comes good character. Since it possesses obedience, cleverness, endurance of hardship, and patience, it is right that it has been made the mount of mankind. As God has said: "And the horses and the mules and the asses, that you may ride them, and as an adornment" — and the conveyance of loads. In India the horse is not bred, and their number is said to be great. They are very plentiful in Arabia, and for this reason Arab horses have a fine lineage. Among its properties: horse's teeth ground up and rubbed on the heart benefit it. Bringing its mane into the house and hanging it there drives the sun's heat from the house. If a mouse flees the house, rubbing its sweat on the hair makes it return. Rubbing on a horse keeps away lice. Water in which a ram's head has been boiled stops nosebleeds if its smoke is inhaled. It eases difficult labor and brings relief. Its fat applied in the ears relieves a buzzing pain. Young goats desire it, and the Arabs keep it, and a young goat follows it. In eating it has the same rule as mutton — whether foal or full-grown. All accept it. Its nature is warm and dry in the first degree. Its special property: its head boiled and taken with something relieves poison within twelve treatments, God willing. Placed as a suppository in the ear, fire applied to it drives away pain. It mostly relieves obstruction. Its dung, if the animal eats the grass of the field, brings on forgetfulness. Black bile and milk with sugar and salt mixed together is good. Its hoof ground up with vinegar and cucumber applied to the head relieves pain there.

And if it is applied over the prayer [spot] with gold it will give health, and if a menstruating woman exists, it keeps away [harm].

Second section: On the mention of animals, and from among humans forty-nine varieties are to be named in alphabetical order. "Ibradi" — it is called the jackal's mine, the eater, known as the Jaloozi, destroyer of crops and gardens, terrifying and harmful. It drives away snakes; if one is taken for three days, the pain in the head will be relieved. If its brain mixed with its bones is applied with boraq paste on vitiligo and smeared with gold, it is well.

The "Ibn Irs" — called by the Arabs the weasel — it resembles the mouse and is like it. It drives breath out through the nostrils by force. Most of the time it causes pain in the mouth and teeth. It is beneficial for people of Kerman. It harms birds and worms nearby. It destroys the brain and is harmful. It is useful for pain in the joints; it ties and binds. Its meat is not permissible and is not useful. It is beneficial when smeared with gold. The "Rutab" — every Turkic and Farsi speaker knows it.

It is healing according to the Shafi'i school, and lawful to eat according to the Mu'tazilite view. It is warm and dry in the first degree, complete in its perfection. When it is angered and many gather together, they cause harm. If one seeks healing, black, yellow, and white [varieties] are known. Its brain when crushed and eaten with olive oil relieves pain.

The remedy should be applied: the naphtha tree of Inzar drives away blood-drinking [creatures]; it prevents epilepsy. According to the Shia school, eating it is forbidden, like lead consumption.
The sana stone, when eaten, expels [harmful things]; it is known as "zanbash," meaning sarkandish.
The golden apple tree: its branches are red, it bears much fruit — called "Jo-lah."
The shokur is called by some a permitted meat, but it is recorded as thorned, though its young are like goats. When buried, it emerges from its thorns, having gone away. Some say it shoots [thorns] at distances, protecting itself from hunters eight times.
It settles in hollows, and when rubbed on the place of hair growth, and others rub it on hair — if mixed with kubr and applied as a coating, it strengthens the hair.
It is said that if cooked in dissolved sugar with water, it benefits those with difficulty urinating.
This green vegetable, when roasted, benefits those with spleen enlargement and weakness, and heals them.
Its pulp, when used with oak gall, is a remedy; it removes certain ailments, and it repels the harms of al-Qayl. Its bark, when cooked and its steam inhaled, increases libido.
It is white, and its dregs, mixed with honey and taken at the right time, produce beneficial results. Its smoke cures fistula and quartan fever — it is well known; according to the Shafi'i school, it is permissible to eat.
Its oil prevents tooth decay, and if the Ethiopian [variety] is correctly identified, it removes quartan fever; if the Ethiopian type is taken with it, the fever subsides. If used by someone with epilepsy, it heals them.
The juice of its molubī, combined with mazer and karawm, increases progeny. "Dharaf" is well known and is permissible to eat. It is known that from its branches and mountain-growing variety, speech is produced, and from its use, various benefits arise.
Its bark applied to the back of the hand, and its branches used for riding animals — a physician notes from its benefits that it is proven [effective].

It is said that for the sake of kinship it hunts and brings prey to its companions. It is well known and its flesh is edible, and its skin is worn as clothing. The saqanqur (skink) produces naphtha when heated by the sun, and if it inclines toward water, it becomes smooth and slender; if it inclines toward the earth, it becomes rough like a lizard and is rarely seen. It is beneficial for sexual potency, and if one takes it as prey, it provides nourishment so that other wild animals and predators do not harm the belly and limbs. It is superior to other organs of the skink. If one places the shell of a tortoise (sulhafa) under the pillow while sleeping, it prevents erotic dreams. It is forbidden to eat and is considered among the agreeable creatures. In the properties of both together: if brought together as a mating pair, they do not cause harm to each other. They are not inclined to mate and from whatever plant they wish to eat, they feed upon it to increase the vital spirit, taking from plants that repel harm and alleviate ailments. It is useful for revealing and healing wounds and throat infections. It benefits those with respiratory ailments and prevents hair growth. If mixed with fire-lizard venom and honey, it prevents the falling of moisture, disperses it, and the salamander (samandar) is known to live among flames, going in and out of fire on its skin and fur. Glory be to the One Whose wisdom and subtleties of creation are without end. They are averse to clothing and garments; when it becomes rough, it is killed. Its venom, when used properly in a bath, restores health. It gives eight powers. The sable (samur) is well known among the Turks, but they desire its fur.

The remainder: the eating of its flesh is permissible. Among its properties, the piebald is well known near the land of Sanja. Its skin is known and its flesh is edible, and its hide is used by people of music. Eating its flesh removes melancholic ailments and eliminates madness. Sanaadh — in form it resembles an elephant in governance, and it is larger with very rough skin. When its young is born from the wild, we know that it, as if we had kept it, would mostly overcome others.

Among the animals, its bearing brings increase of spirit. Its neck is longer; it is found in the regions of Sahnia and among the Arabs. It is abundant in the middle regions. Its urine and excrement serve as a remedy; it is intoxicating for those regions. The smell of its limbs and its body gives a pleasant fragrance and increases greatly. It is found in Persia, in Turkish lands, and among the Khushbaki peoples in the regions of Manq. It is known as Safaha — large among animals. Its young is like a foal. It is noble and among every creature it strikes with water. When it looks at its other limbs, it is assured, and according to its property it is effective as a remedy and healing.

It increases in number and the creature produces offspring. When the Safaha creature increases, the enemy flees from its roaring and scattering. The Dhabb — it is a creature found in the desert. It brings benefit and repels harm through its qualities. According to legal opinion, it is permissible to eat. It is reported from the righteous that the Prophet, peace be upon him, mentioned the eating of the Dhabb — that if one drives it out from between two stones, and its gallbladder is given, it strengthens the mind. One who eats it and is troubled by palpitations and thirst will be cured. If its blood is mixed with flour, it becomes permissible, and it brightens eyesight. It benefits the body, improves complexion, and drives away cold, hunger, and skin ailments, removing them entirely.

The horse strikes and whatever is not appropriate does not reach; and if those on that side are stung by bees, it repels the evil and removes scabies, vitiligo, and blemishes.
Soap: The wild variety is beneficial; leeches remove stains and grease from clothes by night, and if it clings to other animals it kills them; it relieves difficult urination.
Two doses of its powder bring forth what is retained in the womb; applied to the handle it increases benefit. The gazelle: its benefit is for ticks, mange, and itching of the skin.
Its grazing in the thickets is mentioned so that one knows what God has made lawful; it is a counted number.
Its right side is cold and dry; the meat of the young gazelle is temperate.
The gazelle likes bitter and salty plants resembling colocynth; it is patient with thirst.
Its properties: it repels venomous creatures; if placed in bread it silences them, and the musk gazelle in every form resembles other gazelles; it feeds on spikenard and fragrant plants, which is why its navel gathers musk.
It resembles white musk; people compare it to the gazelle.
Its young are very numerous; until those from foreign lands arrive, the local ones serve well.
The temperament of musk is warm and dry; first it must be treated carefully.
It benefits the heart and brain; it clarifies the complexion and brightens the vision.
It removes palpitations; there are other kinds of gazelle musk as well.
Its inner lip is narrow and its nostrils are small; it causes pain and heaviness in the body.

And among the remaining kinds and types, the aura with a single friendship was Tarban. They sought from the dwellers a treasure of the land, and the nightingale was very repelled. If the camel drivers came, they would weave thread through the garment, whoever fell into it until it tore. From the side it rushed to the lizard, the enemy of the serpent and the dwelling place — the mouse is called Fare [mouse] by the people of Lar. They sought the animal of saltiness and mountain, and the robber went, and the mountain tormented and harmed. The record stands as one of the finest of its kind, and among the four, the dog of pardon and the burden, and Talwaj, and the word is there, and they are obligatory to kill, and the obligation of killing them falls heavily. Near the sacred month it is obligatory — the mouse is the destroyer of human life, guardian of the fortresses. They tie a knot and strike the mole on the head of the pardoned one, they steal and the nightingale — they strike, disperse, and the mouse in that place is like a sheep. From the lion and the hedgehog and the mouse there are several types: one type seeks provision through rain, worth a dirham and a dinar, and it loves peace; one type is found by weight and measure — it seeks whatever diminishes with time and hearing and smell, and has more; one type with the armed gazelle seeks and provides, and the graceful gazelle reaches its measure — they call it painful. One type seeks from the slippery ones, one type with the leopard's cub, and one type in the branches. That mouse is of a gentle kind, and its other varieties are harmful to all, and among its properties: it helps the poor, and placed on wounds of dogs, they say it causes them to heal, and it grows hair, and the head — it is sewn onto the hat of one afflicted and cures him, and if it is buried on the ground of someone in pain and bound, it removes the pain, they say.

People, as they sit, fan their wings to greatness and whatever grain they sow is safe. The Manqa feeds on meat and resembles a serpent. It goes to people like a serpent and strikes them; though it wounds its prey like a serpent, it overcomes them. It raises its head in the wilderness and with its peculiar properties resembles a desert creature. It is known as Karkan, famous for being a great one from that place, with its body and particular form of governance. It has the shape and form of a swift creature, well-proportioned in size. Among those described in the text: it drives horses to the ground and in good time reaches three thousand. Three thousand it sells, as it is an animal that fights quickly and harshly, and acts swiftly in combat. It is said to live seven hundred years and similar creatures are heard of; and ones like it are said to live similarly many years. When it becomes pregnant, it carries for three years, remaining pregnant, and the young are born well and strong. In its body it has the likeness of an elephant and the branch of a great tree; it casts them down and the young are crushed beneath. On its own it has the properties of curing ailments and serves as a remedy. Its liver, when given to a person in labor as treatment, is beneficial and extends life. It is prescribed for those with difficult conditions — when given with food and sugar it is beneficial. It neutralizes poison and its strength counters poison completely. It produces a wondrous form resembling something great, with special properties. It is placed among the thousands and breaks branches, bringing down what is above. It increases in those suffering from eye ailments and relieves suffering. It is given to the brain for paralysis and is beneficial, used for various ailments. It is grown again and its teeth and bones and marrow, along with its soul, are gilded and used.

It hunts and seeks power, keeping what it has devoured beneath itself. A pregnant woman will come to no harm, and whatever predator approaches with humility will not be harmed. It is dignified toward females; among the characteristics of kings is its loftiness. The lion, king of beasts, sought weapons, and with that majesty it became one of distinction. Against other ailments, it is a remedy; the crescent white lions are among its attributes. It is terrified of fire, and its enemies are like scattered ants in fear. The musk deer is struck by its scent, and if the musk deer stands between two of them it cannot escape and will be destroyed. In the chronicle it is written: at its second birth it repels those who would exploit it, and from this gold is purified. It is courageous, and repels epilepsy; it overcomes palpitations and great fears. An extract applied repels ailments, soothes the body, relieves springtime fevers and hemorrhoids. When soldiers are bound with its drum-skin, they become like a thousand soldiers. It is well known that with milk and salt it overcomes all things everywhere. When one seeks it and it submits, health is gained and sins are lightened. The river shepherd who goes to the riverbank gives his particular quality to dispel afflictions. For the one afflicted with rheum, applying it as a salve brings health; if a woman looks upon it unawares and one who is afflicted looks upon it, it prevents misfortune. One who is exhausted should lie down and sit, and the veins will be relieved repeatedly. Household pests: if applied around a sheep's head, it cures paralysis. Among creatures, it guides the goats by their nature, endures, and so on.

Mixing barley and similar grains, grinding them together, and if one wants [to use them for] feeding, one should roast them over fire and sprinkle water on the skin.
Fuljah removes the itch, and both [these] medicines are beneficial, and with them [one can treat] various ailments.
In the Jami' al-Hikayat it is written: Among the mountain goats and rams, the wisest and most learned said — a verse — "What a place it is, so that sin upon sin accumulates, and the female becomes domesticated."
From this, what the soul desires will be obtained, as stated in the text. As found [recorded] in the Jami' al-Hikayat wa Nasa'ih:
Abu Bijan is a creature found in India, which they call the "blood-sucker" (khun-kaz) with sharp teeth.
In its nature it has four keepers, and it hunts animals and grows and multiplies.
Wise men have recorded its nature and properties, and it is not by natural disposition that it does harm.
It moves and hunts the prey from the trees, and worms grow on it in the world.
From there it goes away, having captured [its prey], and crushes and destroys and kills it; its flesh, skin, bones and head are broken to pieces. In the Aja'ib al-Makhluqat it says:
The creature called Sawas binds the breath of twelve men and ties their eyes closed.
In the forests and among the animals they gather and make sounds; from these [sounds] they disperse.
They are good at hunting and find their way to Kabul, and their home is in Shadrovar [a legendary island].
In the Punjab it is recorded that two commanders went into a valley, and it branched into seven parts, and in the middle was a hollow, and from it came a sound like the sound of water, and a voice emerged.
From that, animals and birds gathered and those who heard it, when they [heard the sound]...

From these, one makes a catch, and people take delight and bring them as gifts, and one should not let them go freely, for they bring a longing like a treasury that gives what one desires from them by a secret art. The hyena is an animal that is of the kind that the hyena is deceived and caught; it has the form of a water creature with particular limbs, and fire was in it, and it follows and calls out from the plain as a hunter does, so it was not obedient. The army of hyenas set upon that place and leapt, and the hyena became bad and distant from it. It has two hollows and within them it hunts and slays those it encounters, and the carpenters of those places know this. If the hyena was found and what was beyond it was sought, and if its young was found beyond it — it devours its young — and its young and the hyena's cub, some say the Hanafi school considers eating it permissible. If the limbs of the hyena are not present, the broth derived from it is beneficial against chills and is used to anoint houses of pigeons to attract pigeons. One should not place the hyena's young in the house, for they gather there and the burden increases against the enemy and harm comes. The roasted liver, when used with potions of friendship — it prevents defilement and the oil, when prepared, drives away sleep and one rubs it on. Those among the people who are insane become calmed, and it is good for the sanatorium. Applied to stone, it gives sexual power. When applied, another person does not know and does not recognize it, and it removes numbness and afflictions from the body. All reptiles flee from it as well. And if one gives it, that person will be compelled and will become submissive. The Shaykush is a hunting bird of the falcon kind, and since it is capable of training, discipline, and instruction — it is clever and a thief — and its signs and characteristics are explained herein.

The watermelon and the goat are companions to milk, and from its bounty
it becomes softer than the lion's strength — the "Aram" variety
is subtle; it is considered unpleasant by people, and the caravan stops, turning to another direction,
it destroys and ruins, and in the remaining margin it is said that the count
is two — "Arfat" — in the Jami' al-Hikayat it is said that it comes and goes like a shadow and like smoke,
and it appears from the west, stops people in their tracks,
and in one account it endeavors with force to keep people from harm — "Qurtub"
also in the Jami' al-Hikayat is said to be a fine creature of the Karanj, and its breath strikes,
as though the sea floods green and from its breath the air becomes westward, driving things away,
and in the land of Baba there are few of the Hindi kind, found among the Turks, herded and tamed.
They are very aggressive, raiding and hunting, and the mountainous terrain
keeps them busy; they desire flat open land, and they break the earth like a brave warrior on horseback.
The imagination supposes that when that creature approaches, it drives away all harm.
As for Madmash, it is better, sharper, and more piercing than the rest; it is greedy toward children and attacks them.
It gets along with other beasts of prey and causes harm to people throughout the year.
The "Asban" type is known in Majlabi al-Hulw: it appears that the lion and the leopard together hunt
and it is born from among the most suitable and noble animals, and it mixes together.
Alone it finds its way; with its father and its nature it is suitable, and its speed is great.
Dawud said: if it is mixed with honey and salt and the meat is cooked, it is beneficial.
If one eats it, the joints are healed and recovery comes to pass.
It frightens people and drives mice away; goats flee from it — "Qatfa" also in the Jami' al-Hika[yat]...

Among the animals that number around fifty, none surpasses it; it has commanders and a life full of purpose, and no animal is bound by instinct as it is.
