Every creature that is stung by it becomes intoxicated; with the crescent moon, hunters and birds of beautiful form arrange themselves in rows, and they inscribe its names and open its enclosures. Immediately the hunters become drunk, and the white hunters are bound limb by limb. The commanders seek what they want, and the Mongols say: among the most observant and watchful of animals, none is as faithful and loyal as this one — meaning they are accustomed to pulling loads, to accompanying and serving, and to repelling enemies. Even when it goes hunting hungry, though it is famished, it does not forget its duty. Yet its grief does not depart, and the Arabs cite the proverb of the wise man who said: when the dog's bones are gathered together, and the harvest is broken and ground and eaten, so it goes. The hunter says it must be taken by hands and feet, drawn in, and its head subdued and brought out. The best food to present to it is pleasing nourishment. Applying black pitch to the spot where it sleeps causes sleep; black pitch is kept in boots. Those who are tamed make it calm; it is a kind of Turkish remedy, a relief for the chest. Applying pitch to a dead animal for the ailment of suffocation removes the complaint. The people of Multan use it for epilepsy and bind it with the cord of reason. They send their children to it and ask for training, calling it the "cord of reason." It is dangerous and deadly, but it drives away ignorance, fear, and cowardice. Brave men are its sign, and it guides the righteous. By the mention of God, the traveling bags go forth, and the names of places quench thirst like water. This is recorded in the Jami' al-Hikayat: whoever reads it carefully will find its sting to be sound instruction.

The scorpion of the west is counted among those that harm people, and from it comes a venom like the sound of an Iraqi flute. Its origin is from the mines of a place called Fuhara. It is large and round, with a hunched form and a diminished appearance. It moves sluggishly, and if it bites anything smaller than itself, it kills it; it is associated with snakes and with wind-sickness. It hunts desert animals, and when it has made its kill, it stays three nights near it and drives away mice, gathering them with its venom. The beneficial extract from it increases vision and prevents numbness in the limbs. It is a remedy for numbness and paralysis; applied as a poultice it restores health to the bones and relieves pain in the side. Mixed with turpentine and marcasite it stops urine retention, relieves hemorrhoids when applied as a compress, and repels their discomfort.

The fourth chapter: Mention of the great whale of the seas. Take two parts of the extract and one part of white sandalwood; administer it to the sick with the appropriate preparations, after which bring it to boiling and use it as a drink. Its temperament is cold and balanced, and it is beneficial for weakness; it repels snakebite and the sting of scorpions in hot regions. It grows short in the warm seasons of lowland areas, and like hornets it gathers near water. Its venom is known and it has no easily available cure; it increases vision and prevents diseases that are hard to treat, strengthening the organs and curing dropsy of the abdomen, and removing darkness from the eyes. It is a relief for humans, and when rubbed on by its owner it provides protection. It soothes agitation and repels its venom.

Regarding the rabbit: placing its head-ash on top is useful for treating skin ailments. Grapes are good for the stomach. The flea (barguth) is Turkish for...
[It inhabits] various creatures, and its generation lasts as long as its life; from its early stages it remains among them.
Then, drawing benefit from its nature, the great [creature] known as Nughban — enormous in form, vast of mouth, with many teeth, gleaming, dwelling in the highlands —
[It] is like a serpent, having attributes of the viper, and in its nature is [found] in India.
It feeds on sulfur by day; in the world of creatures it is considered a great [being].
The serpent lives and its age reaches one hundred years; they call its young by a name, and when it becomes large it is praised among the animals.
Its voice is pleasing and it travels to distant lands, and in every region it is extraordinarily large.
It reaches such a height that it rises a thousand cubits above the fire, and it draws fish out of the sea.
And every time a wave of the sea arises, like a great rushing noise, it resembles [it].
And it goes and comes and settles near the sea of Gog and Magog and throws into it the blood of men. Its beauty and the voice of Gog and Magog — one must keep people away from them.
As punishment for their existence, from the flesh of unborn creatures they live on, and it is no wonder.
They take from the hearts of the young of the rocks and mountains; they drink it and cause destruction, and thus they settle.
At this time the locust (jarad) becomes the food of the flesh — the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Two things from the water and two things from the land have been made lawful for you: from the water, fish and locust, and from the land, liver and spleen."
Salh [dung/droppings] — a creature very numerous; its meaning is its wing-spreading, and its meaning also is that it gathers together. The locust lives in long open places, as stated by the master.

Zabil was [effective], and its smoke repels hemorrhoids and relieves difficulty in urination; a poultice of senna is beneficial. The scabies [plant]: sunlight on it is like bran, brightened by the light in early spring. The louse-bane [plant] of Sind: it drives away the louse of Sind, stays green, and when it intends to harm the marrow, it is applied between the flowers, taken up for three nights, rubbed under the tongue of the afflicted one each day. It renders the epileptic free of fits and relieves him; it is blown from the clouds upon him, and on such a day it is brought and scattered. Its bark is like patience-herb [sabr]; bring it prepared from the people. It protects from fire. The earwig [harqas]: it is mentioned in the Wonders of Creation [Aja'ib al-makhluqat] that one is safe from the large scorpion; at the time of its destruction, it raises two [antennae] and brings more moisture than rain into the skin of the one who carries it. The jerb-worm: it is a tiny, very small creature called "jalu-man"; it is a worm found among the rocks and riverbanks and riverways. From water it draws gold from the forehead, preventing corrupt matter; the "khamad al-qahan" is a terrible and weak creature of the river. When it has a seizure [sara'], it strikes the stone [and dies]; the viper. The Turks call it "nilan," meaning "the one who peels"; it is the most bitter and sharp-clawed of animals, burned by fire, and its single bite kills; whoever kills it — the Prophet is reported to have said: "Whoever kills it will have good deeds credited to him." It is related from Ibn Abbas that they said: "Kill the two vipers." And whoever leaves them, he is not of us. It is said: "Kill the serpent and beware the footprint of Satan," meaning Satan hides in their heads; it harms and whispers to the children of Adam. Upon Islam, 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said in the text: "Whoever kills a snake is as if he has killed an unbeliever, and whoever kills a large viper is as a warrior." By the intercession of 'Ambar, it is reported: 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas said concerning the killing of [snakes]...

The turtle (land tortoise) is found near every river and has a firm shell, and its size is estimated [thus]:
It has many varieties of snakes — the Arab snake, black and white, long-tailed and restless.
The constrictors bind [their prey] and snakes shed their skin every year.
The spots that appear on its back indicate the number of years of its age, and [each year] a new ridge appears.
After one hundred years it attains [a certain state], and the count of its [natural] qualities [grows].
It leaves no trace; as for the ants, worms, and scorpions, they roast and eat them; and the male sea-snake
— when one encounters it in a thicket, it seeks a pleasant resting place.
If the wandering snake approaches the crescent [moon], the four kinds of snake are distinguished; the first type
is the common one — it approaches from near the crescent and lures from behind, striking the snakes swiftly.
In the western regions and the land of Zarkistan they are called by various names and [are of] different kinds.
Thus it has been related that among them are those called "the biting ones" — the sixth [section].
Second: the karba — it approaches and spreads like the crescent; it is of the fourth type, called "the one."
It has no venom, and the sixth [type] resembles it; but its first [bite] is like the example of a venomous snake.
It has no antidote, and it kills instantly. The second [type], if one wishes to be treated, takes a long time.
Third: the one that has half the venom of the royal snake — it is [also] venomous, and
its nature is not easy; whoever walks upon it, the ground turns green wherever it passes, and [creatures] remain there for some time.
Its color is like lavender and rue, and its kind does not multiply; it strikes and gives birth.
As for the properties of the one whose flesh, when eaten, cleans the interior and is beneficial to the skin —
it strengthens digestion, expels phlegm, cures dropsy, and relieves hemorrhoids.
And the fat of all [snakes], when smeared upon [oneself] with incense — it is beneficial and [used as] theriac.

On the side of singed [material], when rubbed smooth, it removes the cloudiness of the eye (sabal) and pain of the gums. Eating its powder, if a person with tooth pain uses it annually, it relieves that pain; rub it ground with water.
They rub it and it acts: it is best for redness, it benefits those with poor eyesight, like a roast, and— those who eat it with vinegar sauce, prepared and returned, and dried and ground— it benefits those giving birth during labor and delivery, facilitates childbirth, reduces excess fat, and is useful for the elderly and the weak.
It strengthens and, with its juice tied as a compress over the face, it benefits from intercourse. Earthworms with galbanum and khatā juice, in equal parts prepared in fat, are fastened and rubbed as a plaster over the affected part, and a coating of gold is applied, and it is taken as a journey-provision at the time of the month.
Description of the cure for blindness: drink its water and the juice of narcissus; it is beneficial for eliminating putrefaction. It feeds the strong, and those who boil it and apply it as a golden coating find relief. If it is applied in a poultice, it moistens and softens; from it one is freed from [ailments], and in the midst of Syrian and Roman [peoples] and the servants— wherever it is spread, its powder is drunk, it removes the pain of lentil-colic and soothes the stomach, and it is like a perfume. Mix it with aromatic herbs, take it on an empty stomach, and rub its ash into— they call it a great smoke, with a little water for relief, and they read it aloud, and it is beneficial.
First, the dried [herb]: smear it on the body, and paint the surface with liquid gold; the smoke of pain is needed. It has been said by the Persians: crush it, request it to manifest for the Persian understanding— it is called "Sabh" [i.e., the herb]. Its composition: bind the heart. Hold a council for the Arabic method, with the silk foundation of Ibn Sa'd and warfare. It was said, in consuming and drinking: among the people of Marw, its conduct is excused. From the mucus of the silkworm, it refines and delicates the embryo in such a way— glory be to the Creator Most High! That keeper of breath, as it has been said, holds back water from the women and [helps] those giving birth.

One must guard the nest carefully so that the warmth of a human body moves within it. Every day one should wash it with water from the river, and the birds will come in flocks. Several young ones, about three chicks, will become occupied with it for days, and they will be nourished with fine worms; the young will move and stir, aided by warm moisture. Each finger-breadth, one by one, will be measured, and the silk will be produced when they are ready. If the atmosphere and the movement of the air is such that it is dry, the birds will arrange it in rows and will not fly away. If the weather is warm and moist, the worm will burrow deep, creating channels, bringing things up and outward. It will continue moving and rustling until it reaches the proper configuration, and it will go on its way. It will become agile and will make sounds in the channels, and will give to those who tend it daily, so that it does not harm others. The worm dries out and the first servant of Rajab will not let it go from its charge. It is said by the people of knowledge that red and black mixed with warmth and dryness produce a certain humor. Every time one applies it properly it becomes beneficial and produces good quality. It is recorded that its preparation involves coating with a thin layer, and placing some in the middle is recommended. One should apply oil until it becomes fully absorbed, then rub it on sore spots and on the skin. In treating deep ailments, one applies it as a plaster with herbs, oil, and other preparations. It is beneficial and known by the name "ribilah," and it is used as a remedy made from cubeb and aged recitations of the Quran.

It is called "bazdakh." When it falls upon the limbs of a human, it causes great pain throughout; it paralyzes the hands and feet, and the sting renders the complexion and face sallow and yellow. It produces faintness, is foul and unpleasant, and causes a cucumber-like swelling. It quickly afflicts both jinn and humans; one should not be hasty in approaching it, and a lament is heard when it subsides. Leprosy (sam abras) — take it with water; it is cold by nature and similar in character. Except for the kalanj thorn-plant, wherever it is found, it causes great pain and a foul swelling. It is said that this creature, if placed upon one afflicted with fever, will draw it out and cure him. It expels poison from wounds, and if placed upon a sore place, it draws out the harm from within.

The "shabasa" (a variety of insect or creature): it is of the nature of "sunbush"; many of its kind exist in a place covered with wool. When it falls, it causes a cough. A stiff tree produces its vapors, and each of its parts draws away harm.

"Sib tab" (apple fever/a scorpion-like creature): it is like a scorpion in form, as large as a locust, and renders the body thick and heavy.

Scorpion (aqrab): it is more repulsive than an ant and more harmful than a large ant. It has eight legs, eyes on its belly, and its face resembles that of a snake coming out; it emerges from its burrow. Its sting afflicts wherever the head of it is directed; it stings two at once. If it is captured and placed in the sun until it becomes ash, and that ash is applied — it benefits leprosy and other conditions. It drives out the venom, and its burned and powdered form is beneficial against all poisons as a remedy and as a nutritive application.

He would also bring wonders and marvels in the blink of an eye — sneezing medicine.
It is used as a base, and if from the burning sensation it settles and does not purge properly, it causes fever.
Those of this type are like red rubies; if one ties them around the neck in a certain way,
Food placed before them becomes bitter, reducing meals — they are similar to spiders.
The body becomes irritated and parasites form traps from it, like a coarse rope.
They are girded, and the female spider lives in the rocky place, black, attached to the rectum area.
Hanging it like an amulet enables it to subdue; placed in the morning in the manner described it is sufficient.
On the wing, fever subsides; when applied as a poultice to the affected area with henna it is placed, and the body benefits.
Lions mark their territory, making nests; the marks of the teeth appear on the empty places.
It is accepted annually — red-colored — like a town; within itself it creates bubbles.
It means "to carry outward" — examples of it: nothing is done; from it the horn is rubbed.
In many warm regions it is found; "Fari yazlbin" — they call it the domestic animal of the lizards.
It acts and its venom is real — the "Fansahin" — it is used as a remedy, driving away harm.
It draws it from the throat; if one rubs the belly with it and gathers it from the entrails,
If applied to the urethra it relieves urinary retention and difficulty; if one rubs a child
with it, the person will not become infected; and if Sishel is given in answer, with a stamp it carries away abundantly.
Lizards wish: if taken from that — rubbed on it keeping the agarwood —
When that thing is swallowed and water is put in the mouth and rubbed on a salted sheep,
Those animals from that sheep produce milk and yield. Chapter: On sweat and mange.
It is generated; its color is fine and of good quality — Arabs call it proper and the rubbing is desired.
They wish: if they read it, it enters the womb of the pregnant woman, proceeding from the young girl's entrails.

They should be in the palm of the hand, and cast Shibish upon them; the female scorpion lays two daughters, for when the male Shibir passes the daughter to the female, Shibish passes through it, and Shibir the daughter is of the nature of the king. It produces humoral discharge and ejaculation, and the truth of what God knows — as He said, the Exalted: "Indeed, God has knowledge of the Hour, and He sends down the rain, and He knows what is in the wombs; no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in what land it will die. Indeed, God is Knowing and Aware" — this was the subject of the speech of Muhammad to Salmān, upon him be guidance.

It has length, and in the form of the mule it stands upright; it is forbidden to eat, and it is a hoarding animal, very greedy. It stores food, just as one knows that the throne of the mountain will shelter it; it gathers food for the year, and from that provision it takes from the mountain caves. Its sense of smell is extremely sharp, and it reaches its provision by its nose. If it is warned once, it overpowers the miser's provisions and gives them away; wherever it goes, it can break anything. They take it out into the sun until it dries, then bring it to its place, and wheat grain crushes it, and dung properly bound breaks the wheat, crushed, and the dung is in it. So come, O God, transfer in this meaning to the good of the ways. It is brought back again, hair is removed from it, brought to the dog and to the other matter, so that when birds fly they produce the food of birds from their own kind. It is said: "When God has guided, the wings of people are not cut — may God grant peace." It is narrated: "Do not fight the one who offers peace from among the Muslims; when he attacks a man, extend your hand to him and say: O God, I am Your creation from among those You created; do not deprive me of Your grace. O God, do not punish the repentant sinners among Your servants, and grant us rain."

Record for us in goodness and reassurance — Salman has said: "Have mercy, for we have heard a lesson from it."
We have seen and repeated: the hole is entered by crawling in, and in the hole are like bees.
In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And God has made for you from what He created shade, and made for you from the livestock shelters, and made for you from their wool, fur,
and hair, things [of use] for a time. He has burdened you with a heavy load. Enter your dwellings — we
assure you: Salman and his troops do not feel it. And regarding the rizq [sustenance] in the Wonders of Creation:
We say that the lizard's sustenance and form — its head is dark-colored, its blood is cold and it trembles.
The refreshment of creatures: it kills insects and repels snakes and is considered dominant.
It kills and its poison is not intense; it strikes with its tail like a whip, and its flesh is food.
And this thing, when taken as a precaution, brings health and removes spots from the skin and black [marks] entirely.
It drives away cold according to Minhaj, and in terms of falcon medicine it is a [remedy] — and the frog, indeed —
it is harmful and poisonous, and it is obligatory to kill it, and concerning this the Prophet said:
It was commanded to strike it against Abraham, and he said:
"Whoever kills it in one blow, for God it counts as one good deed, and in the second [blow] less."
And in the third: it arose as a plague, catching fire, and it passed — and so it was classified.
In mentioning the chameleon: its limbs are described as resembling those of fifteen prophets.
In books consulted by reliable scholars it has been noted
that it has been heard and reported: the horse-bear [a hybrid creature] appears in the Wonders of Creation — unlike anything else —
If you desire it, its upper body resembles a human and its lower body has two legs
like a human, and it runs on its feet. The horse-bear: in that place a human mated with a bear and a human [was born].

An animal is born without a crest, without speech resembling that of humans, and sheds a great deal of feathers. The kharir lacks reason and discernment, and its speech cannot be understood. "Dudsakar" is a creature found in the islands of India that has a twin body, two heads, and a bridle, and feet like those of a bird; it strikes like a human, resembling a parrot in nature. None of its utterances can be understood, and in its running it is like a four-legged animal, going forth like one creature while lying like another; when it leaps and its feet are weary it rises again and runs on. The "Zagh-sar" (crow-head): in the Wonders of Creation it is recorded that it was brought from India to Baghdad; its head is like that of a human with a crow's body, and however many words are spoken to it, it says: "I am nothing but a foreign crow, I am the lion dwelling with the owl" — so it is mentioned in the Wonders of Creation. God knows best. In the islands of India there is a species of animal with a dog-like body, having two types — one resembling a bird of prey and one resembling a human. They devour people, and such creatures may even overpower humans. The "Sulhafa" (tortoise): in the Wonders of Creation it is noted that in the lands of India there is an animal that walks like a human but whose body resembles stone, old and slow. The "Ta'ir" (bird): in the Wonders of Creation, God knows best, there is a species resembling a human in form, found in abundance, having wings and capable of soaring; they speak, but their speech is not understood by humans — a wondrous thing. The "Ta'ir Arabi" (Arabian bird): in the Compendium of Tales, in the country of Luma, there is a species of creature that also walks upright and has two wings and a tail; in summer it struts like a peacock among people, crows, and causes corruption and harm among humans.

Among the wonders of creation, in the sea there exists a creature resembling a human in form, which has a snout and flies through the water in pairs, and it also grasps things with both hands.

It is said that the sign of this creature comes from animals, and its appearance is described — it is known among people as a wonder of the sea. In the Jami' al-Hikayat it is recorded that a king of China heard about the daughter of the king of Egypt, and messengers were sent to negotiate the matter. A hostage-keeper was appointed and the people were assembled together. It was desired that no harm should come from that side, and after some distance was covered by sea, they loaded the ships and filled them with several treasuries.

The lord of majesty in the port of Misr sent word to the keepers of the treasuries in Basra. Thousands gathered there, and the creatures of the sea came together and collected those things, as was fitting. They did so according to their nature, and the ambergris substance was thus produced — for they are creatures resembling humans in form whose bodies are like serpents. One of them, by the crescent sign, through the inhabitants of Egypt, was thus brought, and a great and wondrous path opened. Word was brought back to the king of Egypt, and the creature came to those shores and to Egypt and arrived at those places and regions.

It is said that since that time Egypt and its surroundings have been desolate, and in the land of Turkestan in the region of Habalb they are also found. They are known as Shinas. In the Stories of the Prophets it is mentioned that these creatures from the time of Moses are animals that resemble humans in appearance. They are extraordinary in their great numbers, and though they resemble humans in form, they are not rational beings and are counted among the peoples of the sea.

They enter and from the elephants come offspring, they bring forth young, they are mute and voiceless, and among them are varieties. One kind resembles the baboon in form, very similar to humans; the elephants grab them and carry them off. They are large, resembling humans in body, having tails, and one familiar kind — their males have no trunk; they lack tails, their hair resembles that of humans in manner, and their form is beautiful. They are more known among the common people by a famous name. The kind with a tail — regarding the male organ — is among the living creatures. Elephants roam freely and are not to be found; they gather in groups and every flock moves in herds. It has been found recorded that in the course of years and ages, elephants have three qualities: they keep letters in memory, they resemble humans, and are like humans in nothing else. They have a steady temperament and no other creature surpasses them in understanding, and they are counted among the causes of wellbeing. If letters are placed before elephants as a priority, they hold them in great honor. Humans also hold elephants in esteem — they are gentle in nature and quick-witted. They make use of them; the first and third are dry, and when they kindle they do not kindle easily, and when called, they respond. When again the birds of flight — it is a wondrous creature, hot and dry in temperament — it mixes the phlegmatic humor and relieves pain and heaviness of heart and palpitation and various illnesses. It is beneficial, and those who are epileptic it brings to consciousness. The river cow — and there are certain qualities: it is unruly by nature, called among the Turks "Mansa Hara" and known as forbidden to eat. In appearance it resembles and in meaning is like a crocodile, resembling it in jaw; it has in its lower jaw teeth, and in the upper jaw twenty teeth, and it moves.

The elephant stands upright and differs from other animals in that its teeth resemble tusks. It has four limbs, wings, a head, and a great body; its length is considerable, and it has a long trunk. The length of its body is eight parasangs, and its head is one-third of its body, proportionate and well-formed. Its ears hang down, and its mouth is low-set and wide, so that the air carries its name far. Birds nest near it, and from its mouth come worms that it draws out from the membranes of its sinuses; within it dwell many creatures that are like lice, and physicians have confirmed this and noted its qualities. It is recorded in the histories of the Arabs that it has both male and female parts, and in some men and animals, such as the buffalo, it causes them to lose strength and become dull. One of its properties is that its presence repels fever and treats eye ailments. Carrying it while traveling brings good fortune, relieves pain in the nerves when applied to them, and counteracts certain poisons. Rubbing it on those suffering from epilepsy cures them; it is beneficial against snakes and other harmful things. It aids digestion and strengthens the sense of smell and perception. In the Book of Wonders of Creation it is stated that in the Indian Ocean there is a four-headed animal that carries tremendous burdens and does wondrous things. Sea animals can go months without food and no one knows how. As for the crab, it is a weak sea creature; its chest is its back, its mouth faces downward, and it has eight legs. It moves sideways; if it is struck and thrown into the air it stays still, and if it falls from a tree or is struck, it is safe from harm.

The places and regions: from wounds, when rubbed on a person like fire it burns. They rub it on, and it is useful for the owner of fever along with moist [remedies]. When mixed together, it is pleasant and effective; hang it from felt and suspend it. They say that under the owner of fever, i.e., quartan fever, it is beneficial. And camphor mixed in a paste for periodic fever, applied to the skin like a plaster, is beneficial and removes [the condition]. From that, like pure wax, it is applied straightforwardly; rather it is extracted from sources and rubbed to clean and remove blemishes from the face. It purifies and whitens the eyes and makes the eyelids bright and shining. Another variety is called "aba'" — when placed on stone it sounds, and it is beneficial for eye pain. This is the tortoise [sulkhafa]. 

The fish [samak]: they say the large fish lives in water and stays in the sea, and it is a great wonder. Every kind comes to the surface and is useful, and it is known as the fish of the sea. There are many varieties of fish. The Arabs pound wood and grain together, and from that they make large ones. The sea fish are caught and measured by the mile and parasang, growing thus. Each variety has a different taste, and every fish differs from another though they come from the same water. Fish bones are valuable and useful at a low price — about thirty-seven types we shall mention. The first variety: the one whose hunting is war [i.e., dangerous], whose taste is [illegible]. The second type [duwwam ab]: its head resembles a hedgehog in shape, black and like... and its two jaws are uneven, like the leaves of glasswort — spotted and rough — and they say when its head is rubbed and mixed with vinegar and applied to the site, it heals.

They attach [hair] and two wings. Third: feeding on its scales is like [eating] mutton. Its white and layered scales are reddish, and its presence brings joy to people. It is among the wonders that if one slaughters it and cooks it, it provides strength and energy.

Four hundred lengths of its measurement, and it is matched against pillows. It has been reported that among the wonders is a fish called "Pita" that has a certain magical property — not only does its slaughter benefit people, but it keeps away harms.

It produces a substance like ambergris, and from half its body the ambergris emerges from within it, and its length is considerable, and amber comes from it. When the amber emanates from its mouth it settles. It is said that the amber is taken from it — it is reported that this fish is large in form, emerging from the depths of the sea. When waves come, it capsizes ships and drowns those on board.

Sixth: the companion fish — it is of middling [quality] and pleasant in taste, found at medium depth. It is reported that it is of large form, twice the size, and when a ship approaches it comes near and remains [there], and if the ship drowns it takes what it can and does not let go.

It emits ambergris and is auspicious, and ambergris from it is [found] in China most of all, in the manner of a fish shaped like a warrior.

Eighth: concerning the fish called "Ud" — its belly smells of ambergris, and when it is time it gives [birth]. This fish is extremely cold in temperament. When it is caught cold, fishermen tie a rope around its fin and bring it to shore, and it is thus bound and its special property goes out from it. It is beneficial in diseases, and it is among those things that benefits one of the spouses.

This passage concerns various types of sea creatures. It mentions the tenth type of fish called Zaz, which is blessed and moves westward with a wide mouth, and like a terrifying creature it attacks ships with force. It discusses a creature called the "Shustar fish" (number 11) which has a large trunk-like feature and whose name is called out to warn others. The red fish (number 13) deceives with its appearance and emits a dark fluid. There is a black fish (number 13) that is nimble and cap-like, which hunters pursue; when they catch it, it releases a dark fluid into the water around it. The Isfar fish (number 14) is straight and its description follows. Number 15 is called Sama, which is known in the sea. Number 16 is a long, slender creature. Number 17 is called Istablan, which is difficult to catch in a net; when it tries to free itself from the net it struggles vigorously. Number 18 is called Muslim fish, which is gentle and soft-spoken and for this reason is caught easily. Number 19 is the Sabr fish, which is small and is found in Indian seas; it can leap out of the water and fly, and it is sweet-tasting and beneficial (number 21, Tarih fish). The Suhnu fish (number 21) lives in the sea and is alert; eating it strengthens the eyes, provides nourishment, repels poison, and cures throat ailments. Number 22 discusses another fish found in the sea whose benefits include aiding the body.

23. The ʿasht fish is delicious to eat; it is found abundantly in Bana and Raha and similar places.
24. The fas fish is enormous in body; some, out of fear, are entirely found in its interior and in its great depth. It enters harbors and bays, and people are harmed by it.
25. The mata fish is very large; its bones are used by people who make polished items from them, and they use its fins as well. 26. The qawq fish has a great head; it is like a serpent that roils the sea and the bays. When they catch it, they bind its wounds and make use of its hide.
27. The kubaj fish has bones under its skin like the roots of a tall tree. It lives in rivers and when it reaches the shore it grows very large; it lays eggs in the water by the riverbank and guards them carefully. When hunters come to catch it, it defends itself vigorously. It provides no benefit whatsoever. 28. The burnuk fish of long fin lives in the sea of Damascus; it has a smooth mouth and it drives away women and children.
29. It has two heads — one in front and one behind — and it has no benefit; it only causes harm and loss. It has two heads and each one swallows the other. It is enormous and is found in great numbers in the sea. 30. It is said that Moses — peace be upon him — had this fish roasted on the shore of the Western Sea, and he ate of it, and from its water he was revived and renewed, and such fish are known to render service to people.
31. In the Indian Sea there is a fish called the karyab; it has a tail unlike other fish and its name is ill-omened. 32. In Hadda and nearby places there are also frog-fish.

The winds scatter and disperse biting creatures, and their buzzing drives away the harmful ones and silences troublemakers. They remove the bad smell — meaning several feathers of a silk-worm — and dryness of the region is a third matter. For trembling and ailments of retention, it is without work; it drives away the harmful winds and by moving about it benefits the joints and the brain. Sugar of age is useful. Also in the juice of the plant, and in the fat, and in the water, it is nourishing and protective and a guard. The skin of the cheek and the mane-hair is plentiful, colorful, and jeweled in appearance. Its fragrance is beneficial for facial palsy, forgetfulness, flatulence, knowledge, and the ailments of wounds and roots. Sugar is useful like balsam, and the cream of the remaining fish. Its fragrance upon white-natured, delicate persons is useful, and its scenting is like pure water. It resembles the harmonious companion, and its sounds and movements drive away beasts, dogs, and harmful creatures. The qustas is a creature, and its scenting drives away things like foxes. It lives in small ponds like fish, going about in the small water. Also it destroys settlements like the Chuklab; its light and garden are upon the water. A black slave rarely grooms itself; it comes and the settlements diminish. Third type: The pain of the flying creatures — the scholars have classified birds among the harmful creatures and have mentioned them in these chapters as more deserving and nobler. But to restrict their types entirely would be impossible; however, it is a sound and correct method as the scholars say. I will mention seventy-eight types, beginning with: Abu Farash — a bird of beautiful form, with red wings and beak, a guide to humility. Its colors are red, yellow, green, and turquoise. At every season it is named after a garment. The chameleon is derived and extracted from it, so they say. Abu Hararan is a bird resembling the goose and that.

And birds gather before it due to its call, and they hear its voice and are drawn to it, and they cannot find a way to escape from it, and the falcon rarely moves.

This is a bird that the Turks desire to eat — it is among the permitted (halal) foods. It is a small bird, more numerous than fifteen to sixteen kinds. In relation to the water-partridge and the heron, it is similar. When it is tamed it can be made calm, and it becomes gentle and tame. If placed under the head of someone sleeping, it causes forgetfulness. Rubbing its brain on a bald spot is beneficial. It is delicate and slender. Its flesh nourishes and increases sexual vigor and relieves pain and is wholesome.

Those who hear its voice should listen carefully — it is recommended for those with ear complaints. With proper care it increases strength by the month, even after years — now for the Turks:

It was requested and it is known to be halal, and from its meat one may benefit. It is known as a bird among the Turks, and it is described as a hunting bird and a trained one. It can be male or female; like a falcon it differs from others and in color. It comes in various forms from different types, and its color is not entirely white nor entirely dark. In European lands it is quite rare. Like a sparrow when it attacks a mouse and drops it from above, it prevents the flow of water to the eye. It is beneficial for inflammation. It is also kept by falconers as a hunting companion. It is called "Basha" — it is a proper hunting bird, trainable and of sound mind.

The meaning of "bursal" in the comprehensive book of wisdom — it is said to drive away melancholy and black bile. In the lands of Syria it is very common. The meaning is that it is a well-known bird among the Turks, whose feathers are bound and used. It is small, related to the sparrow family, and belongs among the birds of Egypt and the Kipchak steppe. It is among the internal organs, and the Bedouins know it well as a remedy. It flies like a small bird and resembles a finch in shape, and among its outward and inward qualities — it is among the creations of great animals, and it has been said that its nature surpasses description. Before the wise scholar, it is known that from a human, it reaches into the brain and causes cold. In a brief summary, its passing is noted. First: it is said to be used in remedies and compounds. Second: the idea is that it provides nourishment for carrying loads, giving benefit. And it provides food and nourishment — this is its third characteristic, and it is as a worm from these numbers. Fourth: observe that it moves according to God's will, and with it knowledge is preserved. And it contemplates like the Hanafi scholars, demonstrating wisdom. It reaches like a fine needle, narrow and subtle, and is not fully mature in its blessing. It can arrive and connect, given as a gift reaching a complete measure and more. Such examples pass through the wise, from those who do not know the divine wisdom of it. Its special quality is found in three ways: it gives benefit in the preservation of proper conduct and refinement. It means "upon the secret" and prevents the eating of carrion like the bird al-bughath. Here we consider it among the worms. It reaches the ground and whoever marks it will be tormented by it and will be punished like the language of — [illegible at end]

It was and it is naught but a sea, and it was said straightforwardly, and therein is stored the pen.
And likewise the old woman's water: if one passes beyond it, one's condition becomes ruinous, and eating camel meat is altogether forbidden.
In terms of benefit, it increases the sight and strengthens the heart; eating it is a poison for those who seek it.
It acts like a scraper: it grinds and spreads among friends, and they find it agreeable.
On a fierce day, in the chapter on birds: it has been given a fine form, with a short neck and curved beak.
Its voice is unpleasant and its morning call has passed away; earthquakes have occurred, and commentaries have been compiled.
And they cried out: the slave of the earthquakes cleared the way, and crowns, and likewise the weapons of war were obtained.
The small bird called Bupot is like a small bird; it is spread widely, and its medicine is recited among peoples.
It is made from horses, and its juice is extracted, and after it is given, the Arabs repeat it and return.
It benefits the heart, it makes the blood wholesome, and it sweetens the eyesight of people and makes it pleasant.
For the month of Zabid al-Nur, it benefits the heart and repeatedly pleases the eyesight of people, if one uses it.
Its form is hot and dry, it surpasses the second degree, and it is very numerous.
It is lethal for those who are negligent, and it destroys crops and is forbidden to eat; its property is like that of a parasite.
Called Chaka: it enters gardens and destroys fields, meadows, and pastures; its voice is pleasant.
It is said: as it rises and descends, it appears on the surface of the water, and frogs come up from it continuously.
As for its special properties, close to it — its special quality: it is a bird that has no feet, like a swallow.
It is somewhat harmful, and by its own nature it presses down; if it is harmful, it passes on.
Its chick grows, and when it is young and helpless, it increases; it is beneficial and it is its cause, and its offspring follow it.
Called Hunari: it is of cranes and of a certain kind; its meat is sought to be eaten, and it is permissible to eat its flesh.
And the birds of the highlands are of the moist kind; it resembles one of the birds; it is advisable and beneficial, and it stabilizes and multiplies.
It grows and, like a chick, settles on the banks, and it is like other birds; it lives with them and dwells among them.

It is from the asb tree, and its fumes, when they rise, drive away green birds from the area. Its inner part, the crop, is dried and ground, mixed with sugar-water. It perfects and cools the excessive heat of the body, and ground with spikenard it is given as a remedy for diarrhea and cough for the whole year, and it makes it cease. It is very good for the crop and the gizzard, and its mention is well known among scholars. It is called by the Persians khalchawaj, and it is forbidden to eat. It is the least harmful of all birds — one year male and one year female. The female is called dud, and it takes the nature of a sparrow-hawk. One year female and one year male — its nature resembles that of a crow, for it carries poison and removes it. It removes pain from one side, cures abdominal ailments, relieves backache, gives benefit to the one suffering from pain, and drives away fatal poison. It is given ground in seven portions. It digests well. The dove known as the pigeon coos and calls, and it is known as the common dove. Its female is known among birds tied to cattle posts. It is warm and gentle; if one rubs it on and feeds it, the bird knows the distant stations and roads and takes the letters far, and its female with it, and they play and kiss and give honey as bees do. The male pigeon from its kind drives away poison, removes intoxication and brings clarity of mind, mixed with pine-tar and tar applied to leprosy — it gives cure. It benefits the pregnant woman, and with perseverance and consistency, it gives complete relief.

It brings it forth below; the air freshens the whole body and scatters its seeds upon it.
It gives benefit against palpitation and colic, and if a man applies it to the urethra it opens it.
And the bladder's stone is expelled outward. Its well-known properties: it has soft, fine feathers on its plumage and flight feathers and is fit for use; it is edible in its entirety.

CHAPTER: It is called by some "qarawush" and is known as forbidden to eat and rich in [qualities]. It lives in mountain valleys, is hard of hearing, wanders through various lands, and settles in other places.
Its fur/feathers are entirely governed by wisdom and cleansing; it is firm and does not harm the brain, and its nature, as was previously mentioned in its proper place, improves the humors.
They apply it to the head like a compress and it does not let the vapors of harmful humors rise to the pillow chamber.
It brings strength and gives good digestion; it provides good nourishment.
It enters and is fortunate, gives nutriment and moisture and is recorded among its species in intercourse. BAT: Some followers of Jesus call it thus.
They wished — and all of Moses's kind made it — and it rained and struck and drove away, and its repellents were thus.
As God the Exalted said: "When you shape from clay the likeness of a bird" — this bird flies in its appointed place.
It is green like the shelter of the sun, and after sunset it flies and eats shrubs, thorns, and the like, and causes harm.
It gives [harm] to the body; it has no hair and is forbidden to eat. Its particular property is: if [someone] throws it into a plane tree hollow, it strikes and kills, and it strikes the walnut [tree] likewise.

[Chapter heading: Deception/Artifice]
Of the trees, two types: if they are bound together, they tremble. If cold water descends upon them, it prevents their movement, and their branches spread out. Their heart stirs from within, and copulation causes their inner nature to move. Their spring is of a sanguine temperament. The Turks, known as the wicked ones, hunt [them] as is well known, like vanished things. The great ones prevent the consumption of game and hunting with arrows as appropriate.

[Section heading in red: Chicken (Dajaj)]
The domestic fowl — the Turks call it: it is sought after, its chicks are desired, and it assembles its group. It is wholesome to eat, its flesh is warm, its food is nourishing and beneficial, given abundantly. Its gathering is good. The rooster comes down to the fence, and its inner nature counters smallness. Its nature is warm, and its chicks come and scratch the ground, turning the soil. When it comes at the time to sleep under thorns, it rests with various colors. After that, all its companions spread out over the land, and the hens gather together with the roosters, strengthening [them]. It gives them sustained nourishment and feeds their inner nature and strengthens them. It purifies like gold and relieves heat on the back and soothes and cools. Wheat-water with roasted chicken and the washing of the scalp is beneficial. Three parts: dry it in the sun with vinegar and smear it on; it soothes. Smear it on sores; it gives substance and relieves lower ailments. In winter, keep it in straw, and in summer, keep it in open land.

[Section heading in red: Partridge (Darraj)]
It is well known; it is a bird of the wild lands, raises its young, and its flesh is greatly delicious, permissible, warm, and generous. First give it delicate food; it is gentle in disposition. In Arab usage, it is served with the finest flavor, honest and true. Among its qualities: it is excellent in kebab, roast, and presented at the table.

It is useful and dispels [ailments], and one who cuts off [ties] from worldly affairs: as Bakr recorded, it arrives and departs. If one uses it firmly as a talisman and keeps the mind at peace, it gives strength of virility and increases it. It also gives help and causes females to become fertile — the heart delights in it, and it is Kharawus Maku, by God. Its rubbing is temperate and dry, and in terms of qualities it is well-known at the proper times. If the rooster's comb is flat and elongated, one should not mistake the times derived from it. The divine vision: God, exalted be He, created the angels bearing the Throne, and they span from east to west, and when one of them takes the king, he spreads his wings and lowers them. He glorifies by saying: "Glory be to the King, the King, the Holy," and when he does this, all the earth glorifies in response to him. I did the same as he did, and the assemblies of those who gather in the folds became light. In the utmost degree it is a great fiery substance, and the white rooster — its crowing drives away demons, and the signs of redness of the throat, and the greenness of the neck and the fineness of the wheat [crop], and its height and grace — if [the rooster] is small and compact and has dry joints, ground and powdered, the smell of it is healing. And if a couple carries it with themselves, it prevents [harm] from coming to the eyes. If placed among food, it enables those present among people to be healed. And if rubbed together with honey, it increases virility and the pleasure of intercourse. The meat of the rooster, boiled with pepper and cumin, drives away [ailments] from the belly and, dried and powdered with pomegranate, brings equal benefits. It is considered auspicious and brings good fortune — when taken in the proper amount by itself, as mentioned above. One should purify oneself, and the belly of the rooster has been mentioned in detail: if it comes to the mind properly, and if one ties up the throat so that it neither speaks nor calls out — beware of this trickery for it increases [harm]. It is forbidden to eat it, and it has varieties: I have seen the walnut kind, and from it comes [a certain] infection.

The earth becomes polluted, and from the sting and bite upon the hand, and the henna coloring on its tail —
On account of this, throughout the days, worms appear and lice multiply upon them.
The creatures hear the sounds and worms crawl upon them, and because of the crescent-shaped creature,
They become like sparrows — if they sit among black ones, the white ones drive the lice away from the body.
They throw them among coals and expose them to fire,
And grind them with honey and mix them and bring out the best, smearing them, removing death, and
Rubbing with kohl stone, applying kohl to the eyes cleans and removes ugliness, improving beauty.
If roasted and ground with a stone, brought out like extract, it improves and cleanses the body.
Applied as a plaster, it benefits and heals. If wolves fall into a vessel,
If one opposes it, and blocks it, and one carries protection and healing —
Take from both kinds of flies: one type that alights on sand and another type of fly.
All of these are of the same kind. The red ones — the birds of good omen — and the salr bird is also of good omen.
In the shape of a vulture and close in nature, it prevents killing. Its bones
It gnaws by itself. The seeds upon the heads of the birds hold the highest virtue. The slug
Harms not; it benefits from the meat of the dog and removes poison from the eyes.
The owner of the cradle — place the scorpion's tail in water and grant relief, and if the owner has a quartan fever, rub with the tail.
Mix the tail with fat and rub it on the face, it is accepted in the presence of kings.
Its large bone on its head, placed in food in small portions,
Give it, and if given excessively to women who are hostile, it harms them.
A pregnant woman who carries it: it is said that the child in her womb will be born a daughter, that is, from...
[Marginal note:] Ash

The chapter on pigeons: what is obtained, and it is a type of pigeon they call; the pigeon has properties. The Dhulagh is well known, large and small — the large one is what the Arabs call a raven (Ghurab), and the small one is the Dhulagh and Dhagh al-Dhagh. They also pound it; it is edible meat, they use it; it has much laxative property, and Abu Qushm — and likewise the Munji when it raises its chick, from its affection it drives away pleasantly. Al-Akhzaz overcomes the raven; burned and powdered, applied as a gold ointment on the body, it restores hair. The raven among all birds is one that harms — one should not make peace with it; grinding it and mixing it with the juice of Munju and Nanjd gives benefit. Its poisons, treated as antidotes, mixed with honey and applied as kohl, remove darkness from the eye. Its crop ground and mixed with honey — two or three parts — as physicians say, applied as a drop will stop watering of the eye. Rubbing the fat on the joints is beneficial and useful. Applying it as a gold ointment on the affected area restores health. The Zadrur is what the wise call the travelling Sar; it is found mostly in spring, in winter in villages and plains, when it rains. Its meat is scarce and dry; salt and vinegar increase its goodness; ground and eaten on an empty stomach it removes phlegm. Its poultice for the head corrects errors and its meaning is known. With leek and pounding, it has the property that is beneficial. The large raven increases nutrition and nourishment; it penetrates and passes through the body greatly. Applying its skin as a plaster on the inflammation of the spleen cures it. As kohl it is taken as beneficial; the Zanbur (wasp) is well known; the Turks call it something else. It has a sting that it gives, and its harm is like that of five askabeen — compound of honey and vinegar.

The season of the horsefly: it drinks water and harms the home like a pest and causes damage. And lice settle on it, and the wasp drives it away, and when it dies it is like a carcass. If it lands on someone's head, they come to their senses. The saqqa [water carrier] is well known; it consists of several fine species. It descends to drink from water, and its beak and mouth are delicate and fine. It takes water in its beak like a bird, and the young ones drink from its mouth like nursing children. The sanana is known among the Arabs and Turks as a village bird, and the Mongols call it the "eater of flesh." Its meat is edible, its flesh is warm and dry, and it drives away joint pain and phlegm, and it is good for travelers and brings comfort. It is cheap and causes no harm. The shaheen [falcon] is well known; the Turks call it "la." It is skilled in hunting and hard to catch, and it is worthy of training and quick to learn. It is good in the field and swift in pursuit, and it is effective against enemies like a pigeon-hawk, and despite cutting away, it returns like a hawk to young hunters. It is loyal and faithful, male or female alike. Noble men desire it. If at night it is given something to eat and its wings are spread, and crushed herbs are mixed and given to it, it strengthens the womb. The shaqraq [roller bird]: it is a provider, a male bird. The sultan desires its blue-red feathers of the shaqraq, and it is known not to be harmed. The shaqraq when caught alive sings beautifully and is pleasant. The shnaf: it is a fine bird, known among the Persians as samnū. It is highly skilled in hunting and worthy of training, and in form and appearance it resembles...

The cold sidr tree becomes visible; a hunter sets out and catches prey; it catches and deprives hunters of their catch and takes away the falcon called Sana and Kibz; it puts birds to sleep by landing in water from a tree and crying out, "I have fallen," so the birds hear it; they come near and find it, and the eating of saffron is forbidden, and in hunting, falconers use the Saqr (falcon), eating of which is forbidden, and in hunting it has full power over animals, birds of the air, and prevails over them; it comes down upon them, and the Dabbakrat bird is among those; regarding what is mentioned in this chapter about the Simurgh: it is the lord of birds, the greatest of them, and its qualities are wondrous; the Peacock (Tawus) is one of the most beautiful of birds, and it is green and red and golden and blue, all present, like musk; no painter however skilled, even al-Mansur himself, could depict it fully; glory be to God, how vast and pure is His creation; the Peacock is forbidden to eat; for nine years it lives, driving away harmful insects like bees; it is among the reasons for attracting honey; its bile is astringent and harms the stomach, and its venom, if boiled with warm water, relieves pain; it frightens flies and gnats and drives them away; it heals ailments, and with its talons it helps its owner; in the land of India it is known as the Kalibala bird; the partridge (Tawhuj) is halal to eat, its flesh is warm and of pleasant odor; it is found in India and in the mountains of Turkestan; it is halal to eat, its flesh is warm and dry, as mentioned in the pharmacopoeia; the sparrow (Usfur) is praised in the Quranic verse, and it is mentioned near the Throne of God, saying: O Lord...

This is the entry on the eagle (al-'uqāb), which has many great benefits. Its brain is very useful and is sought after. All creatures make their nests in whatever place they dwell; men of quality and standing do the same in their homeland. When it goes to the mountains and digs for minerals, it brings back what it finds and restores it. It causes great harm and ruin to those who oppose it, and it blocks paths and roads. The female likewise attacks and strikes with its wings, and feeds its young. It calls from afar and returns to its nest, circling around. The eagle heals sores and ulcers by the force of its gaze, and it keeps the bones and joints well. It forbids the eating of forbidden things and is sought after by the learned and the wise. It can be trained among birds and wild animals, and it is obedient to command. It builds its nest on the tops of mountains and guards the valleys, so that if any creature moves below, it will tumble down. Once it seizes something it does not release it, and if it remains still or moves, it is as if it governs all creatures. It tends to its own welfare and the welfare of others; when it raises its chick, it guards it and nurtures it, and does not let anyone near. Its great properties and the special qualities of the eagle are as follows: if its gallbladder is mixed with nard and applied, it restores sight. If rubbed on the teeth, it stops pain; and if applied to the joints mixed with gold, it strengthens them. Mixed with saffron, sesame, and camphor and applied to the joints as a plaster it is beneficial. The brain, mixed with aloe and myrrh, heals sores. As mentioned in the Wonders of Creation, it is said that the eagle in the western lands lives on the bridge for a long time.

The black shadow descends upon the water and catches fish, seeking vengeance from the descendants of those it has slain.
The Anqa (عنقا): some Persians call it 'Akkarku' and others call it 'Kalnam the army-crusher.'
It is a bird whose eating is forbidden; it roams forgetfully, possessing precious jewels,
and it strives and drives itself to distraction until the bat flies off and perishes. With its brain mixed with ambergris it is beneficial for facial palsy; its brain benefits the mind and heart,
and the smoke of its burned feathers, when breathed in, and its fresh dung when used, benefits the scalp and causes it to grow hair.
It blinds those whose eyes it gazes upon. It is called the Anqa, and it is described in the Book of Wonders as one of the most remarkable of birds,
for it is a bird of such great form that it rises easily into the air, and it was the first bird of its kind.
The ancients say that when it catches its prey it presses it and wrings it out,
and with half of it feeds itself. With such qualities it is said to live the longest life — some say
seven hundred years, others say it lives three hundred years, and for three hundred years
it brings forth its chick from the nest. In the commentary of al-Kalbi it is stated that the Anqa existed in the beginning of the world
among people, and it was among them until in the time of the prophet Hanzala, son of Safwan, it became known,
and it would take from the Torah and the Psalms, and Hanzala prayed against it saying: "O God, remove it and cut off
its power," and God Almighty answered his prayer and cast it into the surrounding ocean toward the south,
and from that time it has been named Zanjabir. It is recorded in the collections that God Almighty
— exalted be His majesty — sent it to the Children of Israel as a sign, descending upon the Holy House, a wonder.
Two of Adam's descendants are said to have been its riders, and it was made forbidden to other birds as well.
By God Almighty's decree, it was driven to the surrounding ocean in one of the remote regions,
and from that time people disappeared and it vanished. And in the Stories of the Prophets and other sources it is related
that in the time of Solomon, peace be upon him, it appeared for the purpose that is described, and it spoke with wisdom.

On the crow (ghurāb): Solomon (peace be upon him) — it is said — came between the king of the West and the king of the East, Lebanon and Amman, and settled their dispute and reconciled them all. The king of the West's daughter came, and he brought her to his horses and raised her. The king of the East, Sinruqrahus, sent his daughter to him as a gift, and a bond was made between them — he placed a feather of the simurgh between them as a token to ward off melancholy. It is said that for this reason Solomon (peace be upon him) summoned the simurgh from its place and had it present itself at his court, and the simurgh appeared there before the people, hidden from ordinary sight, called "Kalāgh-i Farāgh" (the crow of the void), forbidden of speech. From every direction travelers came and brought their daughters there, and the crow remained. As for the raven (ghurāb): in The Book of Wonders it is said that a male and female live together and are very affectionate with each other. When one of them dies, the other never again mates with another, and reserves itself for that time — it remains restrained, and both animals are thus distinguished. When the female has hatched white chicks, the mother leaves them — God Most High provides for them — and when she sees them feathered and gathered, she strips off the white feathers and brings black ones. The chick is then brought forth, and some of these words in Arabic: the black crow is called "Tāhām" and "Samandar al-baqm." The crow called Haytham — the Haytham clan among their people — is considered blessed and brings good fortune. If dried and made into a powder and drunk with cinnamon, it plants love in the heart; mixed in red — [illegible remedy] — it prevents headache; and placed in the house, it keeps away the evil eye.

They give [it] for a year and the cough is relieved. A redness [called] 'uranqi' — stretch it long.
In winter, gather two portions and bring them back from the forest; the male and female come back.
They go to work and sit [in wait], and on top of the hunting [birds] they were fastened, and the feathers [are used].
They are set up green until they knock it down, and when it catches [it], it leaps and runs.
It is settled — thus the diver [ghawwas], the fish-eater, the beautiful Ishaq-colored [bird].
Dead fish are cast upon the water; when the fish see what appears to be dead, they come closer.
Thus it is done. And if a crow comes and overpowers it, the fish come from nearby.
The crow brings [it]: when the crow intends [to catch] a fish, it dives its feet down.
And it waits [some time] until the crow carries [it] away — its feathers and body, moving quietly.
The owner calls it "Nastaki" — they say it does not go far. The fakhta [dove] of Marw.
Some crows, of the type called "al-matawwaf," called out and when their call was heard, they struck.
With pigeon blood and [other things], the sparrows — living — when they hear the sound, they cut and come down.
And in sleep it does so. The "frash" [moth] — some say "gharash" — is what they call a butterfly. And the gharos, when...
It is brought out, and some say it is carried away by the fire, and it goes back and forth.
The candle — it throws itself upon it and is not killed, and it rubs. Sa'di — may God have mercy on him — said:
Verse: I have the scent of Adam; when I detected the virtue, I heard that I should be like a moth to a candle — it said:
O color of green meadow, what complaint is there against the beloved? Do [it]!
O faithful, wretched one — from me my youthful springtime has gone. O the best of companions, from my own youth —
From me it went away — Farhad-like, fire upon the water went — my love grew.
She burned me — it said: from the foot of the fire I was burned. The partridge [qurqbur] is a mountain bird.
Black, sitting in a corner, on the rock it rests; the serpent [samban] makes it tail-less.

One should know that it is among the remedies derived from zaq [a bird]; it is used for pain and ailments. It appears on the surface of water within fourteen days, and relieves afflictions. It settles the restlessness and brings joy. Before slaughtering, one should recite the words of supplication. It is counted among those birds that are sweet-natured, and its meat is agreeable to the palate. The Arabs and others call it by various names; it is considered wholesome. It is one of the creatures with complete character; it is warm and gentle by nature, and from it one derives great benefit. It is found in close places where it tends to stay, and when the crescent moon appears, it mixes with the humors and makes the body well. It is grilled and served with various condiments; it benefits the people. It is believed that its broth is useful for dropsy, and scholars have named it accordingly. It has a pleasing appearance; it is placed on the head for certain ailments, and when grilled and prepared with barley and herbs, it produces beneficial effects. It is known that this bird hides in the wilderness, and travelers coming from Medina have reported it. The Prophet (peace be upon him) said regarding the people of this land: "Glory be to God." It is placed on the gums and given to those who need it; grilling and serving its meat is prescribed for dropsy. Its composition is beneficial, and its bones are used for certain purposes in the manner of gilding. It is known as "qariba," a well-known pasture bird; its preparation involves washing and blessing, and it is wholesome.

The sound of the shikra-bird fills the sphere of the moon-dove, and from that dove beneath the moon it brings forth, and the quail, it is said, produces a pleasant call, and this is well known.
The Indian sandpiper has a long beak and many holes; when one comes out another enters, and it produces a whistling sound like fire in a place.
When the male and female meet at migration time, they strike their beaks together until they grow large, and their wings interlock.
Out of a hundred of their feathers, fire comes to their heart and ignites, and every cage is burned by that; upon that ash the wind and worms pass, and upon that cooling ash they grow large again — thus the phoenix grows anew. The scholars of the greatest waters mention this in their summaries.
Among birds, the lute-players have made it into music from the call and extraction, calling it Qu — the great singer.
The crane (kurki) and the partridge (kalik) are edible birds, large and graceful. They desire to eat worms and insects, and the hoopoe (hudhud) is their companion.
The taste of the chameleon, mixed with the dung-beetle's water and brought with its feathers, mixed as a remedy for the affliction — it benefits those with colic and throat problems, and if applied to one side or the other it is useful and serves as protection from fire.
Likewise the body fat and flesh of the bird: its broth is wonderful; if cooked in water with its own juice, it cures deafness and muteness, and the partridge bird is of good repute; it is certainly well known and leads the way.
It is well-trained and obedient and is known and forbidden to be eaten.
The stork (laqlaq): others know it, and it has enmity toward snakes; it catches snakes mid-air and carries them aloft, and strikes them to the ground and beats them. The storks are remarkable, and our account of the stork continues thus.

The babri (a type of falcon/bird) is perplexed and does not know how to swim, and when its chick is well-formed and of good stock, it takes care of it, and if a poor bird comes down from the air and drops near the chick, it places the chick down. The voice of Hawa is established, and its chick is kept warm by it, and it is one of the best.

Maa Allah al-Hazin (the Heron): This bird is called in the language of the people "Ma Akul Allah" (What God eats), and it is covered. It has been called forever "Maa Allah al-Hazin" and always passes along the waterways and rivers. Its nest is ruined, and when it dives into the water it destroys its nest with grief.

The bird known as "Saka": This is a bird that stands between the two shores, with enmity and hatred between them and its chick. It feeds its chick, and the chick drives it away, and it remains singing of grief and loss.

Its songs are from musical tones, and some say it sings for joy. It is said to be forbidden from eating and its life lasts a hundred and a thousand years. It has a certain quality that, when it flies over cedar trees and beyond, it causes their destruction.

When it eats meat, it gains health and strength, becomes fat, and smells of flowers and perfumes and is not harmful. It repels harmful spirits and protects travelers on the road. When placed in water with certain other things, it strengthens the body sevenfold.

When taken and mixed with water and dissolved, it is beneficial for the body. Mixed with honey, salt, and other spices, it strengthens the body and purifies it. It is placed in the bowl as described.

The Khalaj people, called in Arabic "al-Afani," consider it forbidden to eat, and it is indeed prohibited. It has little benefit and some harm, its smell drives people away, but it also brings something, and eating it is forbidden.

The ugly [bird] of Zabulistan — when it is used as a remedy, it brings silence and healing. Its poultice drives away humiliation; food prepared from it becomes better; its lowly body is bound.
Its water drives away worms; it is considered praiseworthy and fragrant.
And the hoopoe (hudhud) of India is known — one does not eat it and killing it is forbidden.
As recorded in al-Masabih, narrated from Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, the Prophet, peace be upon him, recognized the killing of the hoopoe. [There are] four things that remove hardship and phlegm: the hoopoe, the shrike, and the hoopoe again — the hoopoe is one of the special birds.
It is mentioned in the Stories of the Prophets: "He came like a yoke upon the neck." It carried the secret and disclosed to Bilqis's people and sent messages.
In the correspondence of Solomon, peace be upon him — with the counsel of the holy scripture — it is said that he found a woman who rules over them and has a mighty throne, from all peoples. "Do not kill the hoopoe, for it was Solomon's guide to water." Among the wonders of creation it is remarkable in every place.
He freed himself from reproach; thus the hoopoe came and did its work — a great achievement was found. If it appears to someone in a dream, and if to the dreamer it brings a message, it gives knowledge and eloquence to whoever carries it. It gives sexual potency; the hoopoe roasted and eaten with oil twice — made into a bond of friendship — so that they do not part. If for three days a paralytic or stroke patient [uses it], it will restore health. And it has been handed down that placing its feathers [as a pillow] straightens and sets things right.

The essence that unfolds existence speaks through the tongue of the intellect, saying: "Truly, the Imam is the intellect, encompassing all things, knowing with the Prophet before its very being — the spirit." Just as the ancient masters explained, the essence is a particular thing endowed with noble and exalted qualities. And let one reflect upon the eight prophets of Adam, in the sense of a gesture and an explanation of knowing, and the ruling of the hadith: "I made it, and whoever knows it knows it, and whoever is ignorant of it is ignorant of it." It governs the intellect, livelihood, sight, thought, and every matter — inward and outward, secret and manifest. In the view of the prophets, it never dies and never passes away. God said: "Do not think of those who were slain in the path of God as dead; rather, they are alive with their Lord, sustained, rejoicing in what God has given them of His bounty." And not the least of the prophetic treasures is witnessed and confirmed by the saying: "The believer moves even among the cities," and the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Believers are not those who merely transmit, but those who are transformed" — calling toward the eternal abode. And Ali, peace be upon him, said: "You were created not for this world, but to be transferred to the next." That is to say, the material that is the origin of the drop of Adam passes through stages: clay is refined, becomes fit as food for the human body, and the drop, having become suitable, settles in the womb; there in the womb a form takes shape, pure, and it reaches our bodies — and so it passes through, and we are nourished, and it arrives at paradise with His pleasure, and vision is attained. The Glorious Word has judged it thus: "We created the human from an extract of clay; then We made the drop a clot, then We made the clot a lump, then We made the lump bones, then We clothed the bones with flesh; then We brought him forth as another creation — so blessed is God, the best of creators. Then after that you shall surely die, then on the Day of Resurrection you shall be raised." And the companion Azar Salim has reported: "The creation of each of you is gathered in his mother's womb for forty days as a drop, then it becomes a clot for a like period, then it becomes a lump for a like period, then God sends an angel to it, and commands it" — and so it continues.

And from the Moon it passes through a narrow passage and appears in the world. And they say: if after six months the moon is in Kabul in the seventh month, there will be a hundred and ninety days in the womb. And if after seven complete months it is born in the eighth month, it would have been twice in the womb. And if after eight months it appears, it will be two hundred and forty-five days and twenty-one hours. And if birth is after nine months, it will be fully formed, seventy-two and three days, five hours. And they mention the eighth month and say that those who know the Shia tradition record that for four years and more, it remained in the womb, and it is said on the authority of the scholars that Idris was born four years after his passing, and al-Shafi'i al-Muttalib also said: more than the full term in the mother's womb. And Ali said: it may reach its full state, and thus it descends and is delivered, and the aim of Jesus is attained. The statement of the witness Ibn 'Unust says that in glory it will be born, and according to the belief of the Mongols, Genghis Khan and his brothers were born from the belly of a woman of spiritual light, a noble mother. And Abu Ma'ni is among the brothers. So when the human form receives the command, the soul's place is nourished from the physician's discourse, and from the moment of the drop's fall the arrangement is set out. And when the animal soul arrives at that moment, the arrangement of the limbs and surrounding parts is completed and made clear, and the brain is given as the highest place, as the head is the chief of the limbs. And the resting place of the animal soul is there, and from the moment of creation, existence begins.

They were such that when coldness from the heart reaches the brain and from the brain coldness comes, and through the balance of both, the animal spirit settles, and from both spirits by means of the form they receive, the place of the decline and passing of the human being is from the time of birth onward. In the body, the manifest animal spirit acts and keeps it fresh and alive. And upon the attainment of the rational spirit, it governs the animal spirit and they together perfect the human being and protect it from the decline and passing. They remain subsisting in form, and the intellect, through both of these spirits, and what some call the supreme intellect, is described as a great gift — it is the grace of the Divine — and another kind is acquired through experience and practice. The greater part of the nobler intellect in people is rare, and its manifestation requires certain instruments. It cannot be achieved through these five degrees unless one practices and makes them manifest. The philosophers have said: the establishment of the intellects — whoever receives the lordly grace and becomes endowed with the noble intellect through seeking and perseverance in practice, reflection and contemplation, and withdraws from this world and the next, God guides to what is right and shows the way and the path. A physician who looks at the constitution and temperament gives the body life for forty-five years and maintains it in good order until forty years, and after that it is as the prophet said, may God's mercy be upon all. As for the decline after that, the body weakens and the powers begin to deteriorate, and when the midpoint passes, deficiency sets in and strength fails, and ultimately death and corruption become inevitable, the body diminishes and that is the utmost end.

Fourth section:
The constitution varies according to temperament and proportion: the form of the temperament is the form of its nature and warmth.
Excess and deficiency are not proper in anything: seek the possessor of the image, for that is what is sought.

The animal and natural spirit comes into the nightingale, and if it departs, the nightingale flies away and the body becomes weakened and falls ill. But as for the human and universal souls, when separation occurs it happens in many ways: if the separation is brief, it goes into sleep, and the reason for this is that the digestion moves from the body to the brain, and the brain becomes clouded and the senses are weakened.

When the human soul departs in sleep, the spirit of the higher world comes and perceives things, and sees dreams, both good and bad; the clarity and turbidity of the dream depends on the clarity of the soul's connection. If the soul's clarity is such that its attachments are dispersed, the dreams are clear and true — "give good tidings to the believers in this world" — and the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "The righteous dream is one forty-sixth part of prophethood." And if the soul's clarity is troubled, the dreams are confused and cannot be interpreted properly.

When the soul is overcome by death, it remembers what it used to hear and see in its life but could not retain, and the truth of God Most High is in this. The highest thought is the best, and the most exalted are those of the people. The pure soul's thought is higher and more exalted, and the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "An hour's reflection on the servants of God is better than sixty years of worship." The Commander of the Faithful said: reflect on the passing of life and the loss of the soul.
